# Intake brief — Collect power-up drops on first ship-hull contact with the visual bubble (AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4)

## Problem statement

The player must fly almost into the centre of a power-up drop before it is collected. The on-field drop is drawn as a glowing neon bubble of radius `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE × POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR` (16 × 1.4 = 22.4 px at full scale), but collection only triggers when the ship hull reaches the *icon* edge (`POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE × scale` = 16 px). The result is a visible ~6.4 px "dead zone" between the bubble the player sees and where collection actually happens. Drop collection should trigger as soon as any part of the ship hull touches the power-up's visible outer boundary.

## Users

Primary user: the player, who judges pickup range by the glowing bubble that is drawn around every drop.

User stories:

- **US1** — As a player, when I fly my ship so that its hull touches the glowing bubble around a power-up, the power-up is collected immediately, so the collection boundary matches what I see.
- **US2** — As a player, when a drop is shrinking near the end of its lifetime, I can still collect it by touching its (now smaller) bubble, so the rule stays consistent at every scale.
- **US3** — As a developer, the collection boundary is defined once and reused by every scene that collects drops, so the game and the gyms cannot drift apart.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (contact semantics):** A drop is collected in a simulation frame when the distance between the ship centre and the drop centre is `≤ shipHullRadius + POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE × POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR × currentScale` — i.e. the ship hull first touches the crisp bubble ring. At full scale (ship hull 10 px, drop size 16 px, factor 1.4) this is a 32.4 px centre distance; a drop at 31 px is collected and one at 34 px is not.
- **AC2 (scope):** The same rule applies uniformly in all four drop-collecting scenes: `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsCombat`. No scene retains the old `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE × scale + hull` boundary.
- **AC3 (lifecycle scaling):** The collection boundary tracks the visual bubble at every lifecycle scale (grow/hold/shrink) and respects the existing `> 3 %` collectibility gate; a drop below the gate is never collected even when overlapped.
- **AC4 (single source of truth):** The collection radius is computed from one shared helper/constant (derived from `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` and `POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR`) so the four scenes cannot diverge, and the constant is tunable without touching scene code.
- **AC5 (magnet unchanged):** P9 magnet attraction is unaffected: its attraction radius remains based on ship size (`magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)`) and is independent of the collection radius.
- **AC6 (tests):** Automated tests assert collection exactly at the bubble-contact boundary and non-collection immediately beyond it, for every drop-bearing scene; existing boundary tests that encoded the old radius are updated. `PlayScene`'s collection path is covered directly.
- **AC7 (docs):** `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` are updated so the documented collection radius matches the visual bubble; the current "visual only — collection radius stays `DROP_SIZE × scale + hull`" wording is corrected.
- **AC8 (suite):** The full project test suite passes with the changes.
- **AC9 (documentation hygiene):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Do not change `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` (16) or the bubble visuals (`POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR`, stroke, glow); the fix changes the *collision* boundary to match the existing visual, not the other way round.
- Preserve the existing `> 3 %` collectibility gate and the absorb-animation gating (`drop.absorbing`) so a drop cannot be double-collected.
- Do not alter P9 magnet attraction, mineral collection, or enemy mineral absorption.
- No new art assets (code-first neon style).
- The collection-radius constant must be a single, documented tunable; the adjustment is gameplay-feel and may need producer tuning later.

## Existing state

The overlap test is duplicated across four scenes and always uses the icon radius:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_collectIfOverlapping(drop)`: `hull = SHIP_SIZE / 2`; `radius = POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE * drop.powerUp.currentScale`; `_overlaps(...)`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — `_overlapsShip(drop, hull)`: `dist <= hull + POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE * drop.powerUp.currentScale`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_overlapsShip(drop, hull)`: `dist <= hull + WEAPON_DROP_SIZE * drop.powerUp.currentScale` (where `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE === POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — `_overlapsShip(drop, hull)`: `dist <= hull + POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE * drop.powerUp.currentScale`.

Constants and visuals:

- `src/core/constants.ts` — `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE = 16`; `POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR = 1.4`; `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE = POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE`; `SHIP_SIZE = 20`.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — `drawDropBubble()` draws the ring at `size × POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR`; `drawPowerUpDrop()` / `drawWeaponDrop()` layer the bubble under the icon and are scaled by `currentScale`.
- `src/powerups/magnet.ts` — `applyMagnetAttraction()` uses `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)`; independent of drop radius.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — lifecycle + `canCollect()` (`> 3 %` scale gate).

Existing tests that encode the old boundary (must be updated): `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` (AC3 boundary at 15 px / 30 px), `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` (pickup-radius test). Comments in those tests still refer to an obsolete "8 px drop / 18 px pickup radius" and should be corrected.

## Desired change

1. Add a single shared derivation of the drop collection radius from the visual bubble, e.g. export a helper `dropCollectRadius(size, scale)` (or a `POWER_UP_DROP_COLLECT_RADIUS_FACTOR = POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR` constant plus helper) in `src/core/constants.ts` / `src/powerups/icons.ts` that returns `size × POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR × scale`.
2. Replace the four duplicated `_overlapsShip` / `_collectIfOverlapping` radius computations with the shared helper.
3. Update boundary tests to the new radius and add explicit "collected at bubble contact / not collected just beyond" assertions for each scene.
4. Correct the README and GDD wording so the documented collection radius is the bubble radius, not the icon radius.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — Add `POWER_UP_DROP_COLLECT_RADIUS_FACTOR` (default `= POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR`) and/or `dropCollectRadius()` helper; document that collection matches the visual bubble.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — Export the bubble-radius derivation shared with `drawDropBubble()` (or reuse the constant) so visual and collision cannot drift.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Use the shared collection radius in `_collectIfOverlapping`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — Use the shared collection radius in `_overlapsShip`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — Use the shared collection radius in `_overlapsShip`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — Use the shared collection radius in `_overlapsShip`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — Update boundary tests; add bubble-contact assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — Update boundary tests; add bubble-contact assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — Add bubble-contact assertions.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` (if present) — Add/adjust PlayScene collection-path coverage.
- `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Correct collection-radius wording.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** – Make weapons both cumalative and time out (open) — touches the same `GymWeapons` drop collection path.
- Automated related-work report (see `## Related work (automated report)` in the work-item description) — related completed items: AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620 (Player thruster SFX), AH-0MTECNI1Y001O2OV (enemy live aim tracking), AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q (minerals/power-up choice).
- Precedent for the bubble being deliberately larger than the icon: AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4 (doubled 32 px size / bubble). This intake changes only the collision radius, not the visual.

## Risks and assumptions

- **A1 (collection boundary = crisp ring):** "Contacts the power up" is interpreted as the ship hull touching the outer edge of the crisp neon bubble ring (`factor 1.4`), not the softer outer glow halo (`ring × 1.6`). This is the salient visual boundary; using the glow would enlarge pickups further without a clear visual edge.
- **A2 (uniform scope):** The bug report is generic ("the player"); all four drop-bearing scenes (including production `PlayScene`) are updated uniformly.
- **A3 (magnet independent):** P9 magnet attraction uses its own ship-size-based radius and is unchanged.
- **Risk — balance:** The effective capture distance grows from 26 px to 32.4 px at full scale (~+25 %), making pickups noticeably easier. Mitigated by making the boundary a named tunable constant.
- **Risk — test drift:** Existing boundary tests assert the old radius (e.g. 30 px is "beyond" the old 26 px radius but is inside the new 32.4 px radius); they must be updated or they will fail.
- **Risk — documentation contradiction:** README/GDD currently state the bubble is "visual only"; leaving them stale would mislead future work.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Do not bundle other collection changes (magnet tuning, mineral collection, enemy absorption, bubble visual changes). Any such opportunities are recorded as separate linked work items, not absorbed into this fix.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

The following questions were raised by earlier intake sessions and remain unanswered (recorded here idempotently; agent defaults are stated so work can proceed, but producer confirmation is requested).

- **Q1: Collection boundary target** — Should collection trigger when the ship hull first touches the visual bubble's outer edge (`hull + POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE × POWER_UP_BUBBLE_RADIUS_FACTOR × scale` = 32.4 px at full scale)? *Answer:* **OPEN QUESTION** — agent default: yes, use the crisp bubble ring edge (factor 1.4). Rationale: the bug asks for collection "as soon as a pixel of the ship … contacts the power up", and the bubble is the power-up's visible boundary. Previously asked in comments AH-C0MTXQLNS2001U9XT and AH-C0MU7EO0CN000J4N6.
- **Q2: Scale behaviour** — Should the collection radius track the bubble proportionally through grow/hold/shrink? *Answer:* **OPEN QUESTION** — agent default: yes, `size × 1.4 × currentScale` (mirrors the existing proportional formula, so behaviour is consistent at every lifecycle scale).
- **Q3: Scope** — Should all three gym scenes (plus production `PlayScene`) be updated? *Answer:* **OPEN QUESTION** — agent default: yes, all four drop-bearing scenes, since the report is generic and drift between game and gyms is a known root-cause pattern in this repo.
- **Q4: Magnet interaction** — Does changing the collection radius affect P9 magnet behaviour? *Answer:* **OPEN QUESTION** — agent default: no; magnet uses `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)` and is independent. Evidence: `src/powerups/magnet.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`.

# Intake Brief — Need juice when the player is destroyed (AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY)

> **Status of this brief:** the operator was asked four clarifying questions
> (see Appendix) and replied "continue" without answering. Per the workflow's
> "do not block indefinitely" rule, this brief proceeds on **documented
> assumptions** (marked `[ASSUMPTION]` throughout). Open questions are retained
> in the Appendix for producer validation; the item is flagged
> `needsProducerReview` until they are resolved.

## Problem statement

When the player is destroyed the game currently plays a single particle burst
(`spawnExplosionParticles(...SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE...)`), the shared enemy
`playDestructionSound()`, and a 150% scale pulse, then immediately respawns or
ends the run. There is no camera shake, no player-specific death sound, and no
layered secondary feedback, so the most consequential event in the game feels
flat. The operator wants "lots of juice … screen shake, particle explosion, SFX
etc. Go wild!"

## Users

- **Player** — feels a weighty, unmistakable consequence when their ship is
  destroyed, distinct from ordinary enemy kills, reinforcing that a life was
  lost (or the run ended).
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — can adjust shake intensity, sound
  layering, flash strength, and extra layers through exposed constants in one
  place without editing each death path.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, when my ship is destroyed I feel a strong impact: the
  camera shakes hard, a bright flash frames the screen, the explosion is
  visibly larger than an enemy's, and a distinct low "hull breach" boom plays
  instead of the generic enemy pop — so a life lost reads differently from a
  kill.
- As a **player**, the effect scales: losing my final life (game over) feels
  even heavier than a mid-run respawn, without becoming disorienting.
- As a **developer**, I can tune `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
  `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`, and the dedicated sound's amplitude in one
  constants module, and the behaviour is covered by unit tests so tuning does
  not silently regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Shared player-death juice helper exists:** A reusable helper
  (e.g. `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` or an extension of
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) can be invoked from a scene with
  `(scene, x, y)` and composes the full effect (screen shake + particle burst +
  flash + any additional layers), returning/recording handles so scene teardown
  can destroy them. Both player-death paths use it:
  `PlayScene._loseLife()` (real run, lives/game-over) and
  `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` (combat gym, in-place respawn).
- [ ] **AC2 — Screen shake:** A scene-camera shake is triggered on player
  destruction with a configurable intensity and duration (suggested defaults:
  intensity ~0.008–0.02, duration ~250–400 ms, full 2D). Shake strength is a
  tunable constant in one module. Verified by unit test with a camera spy
  (`camera.shake` called with the configured intensity/duration).
- [ ] **AC3 — Dedicated player-death SFX:** A new `playPlayerDestructionSound()`
  in `src/audio/effects.ts`, distinct from the generic
  `playDestructionSound()` (suggested: heavier/lower multi-layer cue — impact
  thump + descending body + brief noise tail), exposed amplitude/length as
  constants. The player-death paths call it **exactly once**; existing
  `playDestructionSound()` calls on those paths are replaced (no double-play).
  Verified by unit test (call-count + no generic sound on player death).
- [ ] **AC4 — Extra juice layers (assumption-marked):** At least two additional
  layered effects beyond particles + shake + sound, each configurable and
  testable. Proposed set `[ASSUMPTION]`: (a) a brief full-screen white/cyan
  **flash** (alpha fades ~1 → 0 over ~120–200 ms) and (b) **debris shards** or
  an expanding **shockwave ring** that outlive the particle burst briefly. Each
  layer is individually toggleable via a constant so the producer can drop any
  they dislike without code surgery.
- [ ] **AC5 — Severity scaling & no behaviour change:** The effect is heavier
  for run-ending death (final life / game over) than for a mid-run respawn
  `[ASSUMPTION]`, via a `severity` parameter. Respawn position, invulnerability
  duration, blink, lives/score accounting, and shield-absorption behaviour are
  unchanged; no changes to hit detection.
- [ ] **AC6 — Teardown / no leaks:** All juice-owned GameObjects (flash
  overlay, debris, shockwave, particles) are tracked and destroyed on scene
  `SHUTDOWN`; stop→restart of a scene instance leaks nothing (mirrors the
  existing `playerExplosions` registry pattern).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: shake fired with
  configured params; dedicated sound called exactly once and generic sound not
  called on the player path; flash fades and is destroyed; debris/shockwave
  lifecycle; severity scaling; teardown leaks nothing. Existing player/scene
  suites still pass (update any assertions that assume the old single-burst
  behaviour).
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** GDD §7.2 (and §7.3 audio if the new cue is
  listed) updated to describe the player-death juice; code comments on new
  constants/helpers; README updated if it documents audio/VFX behaviour.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes**
  (`npm test` = `vitest run`) and `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`).

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser 4.2.1 + TypeScript 7, Vite, Vitest 4 (existing stack).
  Prefer Phaser `camera.shake()` for shake and Graphics/tween layers for the
  rest, consistent with the existing Graphics-particle approach in
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`.
- **Performance:** must not drop FPS on web; layers are short-lived and pooled
  or destroyed promptly; no per-frame allocation leaks.
- **Neon aesthetic:** consistent with GDD §7.1 palette; player effects centre
  on `SHIP_COLOR 0x00ffff`.
- **No behaviour change beyond VFX/audio:** respawn, invulnerability, lives,
  score, and shield logic untouched; no double audio.
- **Testability:** pure logic (intensity/duration/severity mapping) separated
  from Phaser rendering so it is unit-testable with fakes/spies.
- **No heavy new audio assets assumed:** sounds are synthesised with the
  Web Audio `blip`/oscillator helpers already in `src/audio/effects.ts`
  `[ASSUMPTION]` (no binary asset pipeline in this repo).

## Existing state

- **Player-death particle burst already exists** (shipped in
  AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V, v0.1.3): `spawnExplosionParticles(scene, x, y,
  SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE, { patterns: resolvePatterns('player'), registry })`,
  called from `PlayScene._spawnPlayerExplosion()` and
  `GymFormationScene._spawnPlayerExplosion()`.
- **Sound:** both player paths call the generic enemy cue
  `playDestructionSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:430`, a 0.28 s descending
  sawtooth blip at volume 0.3). No player-specific cue exists.
- **Scale pulse:** both paths tween the ship to `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK` (1.5)
  over `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PULSE_DURATION/2` (0.2 s) and back.
- **No camera shake anywhere:** `grep` for `camera.shake` / `this.cameras`
  across `src/` returns nothing.
- **Two death paths:**
  - `PlayScene._hitPlayer() → _loseLife(explodeShip=true)` — costs a life,
    triggers `_finishRun(false)` at 0 lives, else `respawnInPlace()` +
    invulnerability blink.
  - `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` — combat gym: increments
    `playerHitCount`, plays sound + particles + scale pulse, `respawnInPlace()`,
    sets invulnerability/blink.
- Relevant constants live in `src/core/constants.ts`
  (`PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK=1.5`, `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PULSE_DURATION=0.4`,
  `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE=1.5`, `COMBAT_HIT_BLINK_INTERVAL=0.1`).

## Desired change

1. Add a shared player-death juice composition helper (pure severity→params
   mapping + thin Phaser application) in `src/vfx/`.
2. Add tunable constants for shake intensity/duration, flash alpha/duration,
   debris/shockwave counts/lifetimes, and severity multipliers, in one module.
3. Add a dedicated `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (layered, heavier) to
   `src/audio/effects.ts`; replace the generic `playDestructionSound()` call on
   the two player-death paths only (enemy paths unchanged).
4. Trigger scene-camera shake on player destruction, scaled by severity.
5. Add the extra juice layers (flash + debris/shockwave) as individually
   toggleable, teardown-tracked GameObjects.
6. Wire both `PlayScene._loseLife()` and `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` to the
   helper; preserve all existing non-VFX behaviour.
7. Add/extend unit tests and update GDD §7.2/§7.3 + comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` — **new.** Composes shake + flash + debris/
  shockwave (+ delegates to existing particle helper); pure `resolveJuiceParams(severity)`
  mapping and teardown registry.
- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` — **new.** Shake params, flash/debris
  lifecycle, severity scaling, teardown.
- `src/vfx/constants.ts` (or `src/core/constants.ts`) — new tunables:
  `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION`,
  `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, debris/
  shockwave counts, `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (+ constants);
  leave `playDestructionSound()` untouched for enemies.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_loseLife()` / `_hitPlayer()` /
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` call the new helper with severity `'fatal'` vs
  `'respawn'`; SHUTDOWN teardown updates.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` /
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` call the helper with `'respawn'` severity;
  SHUTDOWN teardown updates (`playerExplosions` registry pattern).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene*.test.ts`
  — update/extend hit-response assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 particle/VFX and §7.3 audio notes.

## Related work

- **Immediate predecessor (completed):** Add particle-based explosion VFX for
  enemy and player deaths (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V) — delivered the shared
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`, colour jitter, three pattern emitters, and
  wiring to all death paths. Its scope-creep guard explicitly deferred
  **screen-shake, sound redesign, debris physics, and trailing smoke** to
  "linked work items if desired" — this item is that follow-up.
- Respawn player in same spot (AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN) — `respawnInPlace()`
  behaviour that must be preserved.
- Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT) — gym player
  presence.
- One Tank changes colour (AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G) — sibling colour-per-entity
  work; coordinates on palette usage.
- GDD §7.1 colour palette, §7.2 particle effects, §7.3 audio cues.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — "go wild" is unbounded / subjective.** Mitigation: bound the scope
  to a named layer set (shake, dedicated SFX, flash, debris/shockwave), each
  individually toggleable via constants; exact intensities are tunable and
  locked by unit tests, with a manual feel pass.
- **Risk — unanswered operator questions mean the layer set is a guess.**
  Mitigation: all invented scope is marked `[ASSUMPTION]`; the item is flagged
  `needsProducerReview`; each layer can be dropped without rework.
- **Risk — screen shake can cause discomfort / motion sickness.** Mitigation:
  keep duration short (~250–400 ms) and intensity modest; consider respecting
  a future reduced-motion setting (not in scope here — record as linked work
  item if the producer wants it).
- **Risk — test churn on hit-response suites.** Mitigation: update assertions
  to cover the new helper call/seams; keep behaviour guarantees (respawn,
  lives, no double-audio) explicit in tests.
- **Risk — double audio regression.** Mitigation: dedicated AC + test that the
  player path plays the new sound exactly once and not the generic cue.
- **Assumption — sounds are synthesised** via existing Web Audio helpers (no
  new asset pipeline).
- **Assumption — severity scaling** ('fatal' heavier than 'respawn') is wanted;
  easily removed if not.
- **Assumption — both death paths** (real run + combat gym) should get the
  juice; if only the real run is wanted, the gym wiring can be dropped.
- **Scope-creep guard:** reduced-motion accessibility setting, screen-edge
  vignette, controller rumble/haptics, score-popup redesign, and full audio
  redesign are out of scope; file as linked work items if desired.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Particle explosions already exist (completed in AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V). Do
  you want these enhanced (more particles, longer duration, additional effects
  layered on top), or is the particle part considered done?" — Operator replied
  "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption: the
  existing particle burst stays as the base layer; *additional* layered effects
  (flash, debris/shockwave) are added on top.
- Q2: "Screen shake — none exists today. Intensity and duration? Single strong
  shake fading over ~200–300 ms, layered, or horizontal only vs full 2D?" —
  Operator replied "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working
  assumption: single full-2D shake, intensity ~0.008–0.02, duration ~250–400 ms,
  scaled by severity.
- Q3: "SFX — should the player death have its own dedicated sound distinct from
  enemy destruction? Layered sounds or a single improved sound?" — Operator
  replied "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption:
  dedicated layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()`, distinct from the generic
  enemy cue.
- Q4: "\"Lots of juice\" — beyond particles, screen shake, and SFX, what other
  juice do you envision? (e.g. screen flash, debris, slow-mo, UI feedback,
  score popup, camera zoom?)" — Operator replied "continue" without an answer.
  **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption: brief full-screen flash + debris
  shards/expanding shockwave ring; nothing else.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX** – Diver should rotate to face the player and dive towards them (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G** – One Tank changes colour (completed)
- **AH-0MTHG5BSP006A81R** – Gym index discovers all enemy configs (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+313 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mtvybl2l0085g6g, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+309 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mtvybl2l0085g6g, ac1, ac4, add, added (+246 more)

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan_complete)

**Decision:** Full planning. Effort is **Small** and risk **Medium**; the bundled
pre-check returned `decision: "plan"`. The plan-approval gate returned
`request_approval: false` (effort not Medium+, risk not High), so no approval pause was
taken — producer validation of the OPEN QUESTIONS below is still requested.

**Vertical-slice phasing:** every item is an end-to-end slice (module + tests + wiring +
docs where relevant); between phases the next item's description is re-checked. Test-first:
the pure parameter model (F1) is the test-first spec that fails before implementation, and
the cross-path verification sweep (F9) closes the loop after wiring.

### Features

| # | Feature | Type | Depends on | Effort | Risk | ID |
|---|---------|------|-----------|--------|------|----|
| F1 | Player-death juice parameter model and constants | task | — | S | Low | AH-0MUDY2GH3003NYY3 |
| F2 | Dedicated player-destruction SFX | task | — | S | Low | AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A |

data.description:
Hitting '?' or clicking a 'Help (?)' button next to the 'Index' button should pause the game and bring up a screen that lists all the powerups available in that gym scene. It will have the icon and a description of what it does.

---

*Migrated from ContextHub work item `WL-0MTPLA9BT008HWVL` (misfiled in the ContextHub project; belongs to AI_Hell).*

---

## Intake brief

**Headline:** Add a shared `Help (?)` affordance to the three power-up/weapon gym scenes that pauses the gym and shows a code-drawn icon, name and one-line description for every drop that gym can spawn, with the copy sourced from the shared catalogues.

### Problem statement

The power-up and weapon gym scenes are the project's primary tuning and demonstration surfaces, but a player or developer arriving in a gym has no way to learn what each drop on the field actually does short of reading the GDD. The gyms need an in-context help overlay that pauses the gym and shows, for every drop that gym can spawn, the drop's icon, its name and a one-line description.

### Users and user stories

- **As a developer tuning a gym**, I want to press `?` (or click a `Help (?)` button) and see the icon + effect of every drop this gym can spawn, so I can interpret what I am observing without leaving the gym or opening the GDD.
- **As a player/investigator exploring the dev gym index**, I want the help to show the *same* icon I see on the field and an accurate one-line description, so I can recognise drops at a glance.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the help text to come from the shared catalogues so it can never drift from the implemented behaviour.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymWeapons` renders a `Help (?)` text button immediately next to the existing `← INDEX` button, and pressing `?` opens the same help overlay. Opening the help **pauses** the gym's simulation (movement, spawning, firing all stop) and resumes exactly where it paused on close.
2. The help overlay lists exactly the drop types the current gym can spawn, one row per drop, each showing the code-drawn icon that matches the in-game drop, the display name and a one-line description:
   - `GymPowerUpsUtility`: P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet.
   - `GymPowerUpsCombat`: P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport.
   - `GymWeapons`: Cannon (permanent default), Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset.
3. Help descriptions are sourced from the shared gameplay catalogues — a `description` field on `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) and on the weapon catalogue plus a Reset entry (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) — so the help cannot drift from implemented behaviour; every catalogue entry exposes a non-empty `description`.
4. Closing the help via `?`, the overlay's `Close` control, or **ESC** resumes the gym. While the help overlay is open, **ESC closes the help and does not exit to the main menu**; once closed, ESC again returns to the main menu as it does today. The `Close` control is focused by default and operable by keyboard (Tab / arrow keys + Enter / Space).
5. The `Help (?)` button is placed adjacent to the existing `← INDEX` button without overlapping it, and the overlay is an opaque full-screen replacement (consistent with `PauseScene`) that is legible at the game's fixed 16:9 resolution.
6. Automated tests cover the shared helper, the `HelpScene`, and its integration into all three gyms (open pauses; content matches the gym's drop pool; `?`/`Close`/ESC resume; ESC does not reach the menu while open). **The full project test suite passes with the new changes.**
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §4.4 catalogue table and §6.4 gym sections).

### Constraints

- **No external art assets** — icons must reuse the existing code-drawn drawers `drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon` (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), per the GDD §7.1 code-first convention.
- **The new `HelpScene` must not live in `src/scenes/gym/`**: gym scenes are auto-discovered by `import.meta.glob('../scenes/gym/*.ts')`, so a file placed there would appear as a bogus entry in the gym index. It belongs in `src/scenes/` and must be registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- **Do not change existing navigation semantics**: the `← INDEX` button must still return to `GymIndex`, and ESC must still return to the main menu when help is closed.
- **Paused scenes do not receive keyboard input** (`KeyboardPlugin.isActive()` is false while paused), so the `?`/ESC *close* handling must live in `HelpScene`, not in the paused gym.
- The overlay is a dev/gym affordance; the shipped `PlayScene` is out of scope.

### Existing state

- The three gyms each call `addBackToIndexButton(this)` and `addBackToMenuOnEsc(this)` (`src/utils/gymNavigation.ts`); there is no help button, no `?` handling, and no help/legend screen anywhere in the game.
- `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) holds P3–P9 with `id`, `name`, `type`, optional `duration`/`maxStacks`, but **no description**. `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) holds `cannon`/`spread`/`dual`/`rapid` with `id`, `name`, pattern data and **no description**; `reset` is a drop type with no catalogue entry.
- Each gym already owns an ordered list of the drops it spawns: `NON_COMBAT_ORDER` (`P5,P8,P9`), `COMBAT_ORDER` (`P3,P4,P6,P7`), `ROUND_ROBIN_ORDER` (`spread,dual,rapid,reset`).
- `PauseScene` (`src/scenes/PauseScene.ts`) is the precedent for a full-screen overlay that pauses gameplay and uses `FocusManager` for keyboard-operable controls; it is registered in `gameConfig.ts`.

### Desired change

1. Add a `description` string to every `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry and every `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, plus a description for the `reset` drop (e.g. a small typed map/entry alongside the weapon catalogue), derived from GDD §4.4. Proposed one-line copy:
   - P3 Shield — "Absorbs one hit; a bubble protects the ship for 15 s."
   - P4 Bomb — "Instantly clears every on-screen enemy bullet (no enemy damage)."
   - P5 Speed Boost — "+50% movement speed for 10 s."
   - P6 Phase Shift — "3 s of intangibility — pass through enemies and bullets."
   - P7 Teleport — "Stores a use; press S or ↓ to warp to the nearest safe spot and gain 3 s Phase Shift on arrival."
   - P8 Extra Life — "+1 life immediately (starts at 3, capped at 5)."
   - P9 Magnet — "Permanently pulls nearby drops toward the ship (stacks up to 5)."
   - Cannon — "Permanent default weapon — one bullet straight ahead."
   - Spread — "Adds a 3-bullet fan (−30°/0°/+30°) for 10 s."
   - Dual — "Adds two side-by-side bullets for 10 s."
   - Rapid — "Adds single bullets at a much higher fire rate for 10 s."
   - Reset — "Clears all timed weapons, leaving only the Cannon."
2. Add a shared gym help helper (proposed `src/utils/gymHelp.ts`) exposing `addHelpButton(scene, { gymKey, drops })`, where `drops` is the gym's ordered drop list (`DropId | 'cannon'`). It renders the `Help (?)` button next to `← INDEX`, and on pointerdown or `?` keydown calls `scene.scene.pause()` then `scene.scene.launch('HelpScene', { gymKey, drops })`. It also exposes the id → `{ name, description, drawIcon }` lookup used by both the button and the overlay so icons/names/descriptions have one source.
3. Add `src/scenes/HelpScene.ts`: an opaque full-screen overlay titled with the gym label, rendering one row per requested drop (code-drawn icon + name + wrapped description), plus a focused `Close` control. It handles `?`, ESC and the `Close` control by `scene.stop()`-ing itself and `scene.resume(gymKey)`-ing the originating gym. Register it in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
4. Wire `addHelpButton` into the three gyms, passing each gym's existing drop-order constant (and `['cannon', ...ROUND_ROBIN_ORDER]` for `GymWeapons`).
5. Update the GDD §4.4/§6.4 and README gym sections, and add code comments documenting the overlay and the new catalogue description fields.

### Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Add a `description` field to `PowerUpEntry` and a one-line description to every P3–P9 catalogue entry.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — Add a `description` field to `WeaponDefinition` and descriptions for cannon/spread/dual/rapid; add a `reset` description entry.
- `src/utils/gymHelp.ts` — **New.** `addHelpButton(scene, config)`, the `HelpDropId` type and the id → `{ name, description, drawIcon }` lookup shared by the button and overlay.
- `src/scenes/HelpScene.ts` — **New.** Full-screen opaque help overlay scene (icon + name + description rows, focused `Close`, `?`/ESC handling, resume-gym lifecycle).
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — Register `HelpScene` so it can be launched from the dynamically-added gym scenes.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — Call `addHelpButton` with `NON_COMBAT_ORDER`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — Call `addHelpButton` with `COMBAT_ORDER`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — Call `addHelpButton` with the cannon + `ROUND_ROBIN_ORDER` drop list.
- `src/utils/gymHelp.test.ts` — **New.** Unit tests for the lookup/description coverage and button wiring.
- `src/scenes/HelpScene.test.ts` — **New.** Scene-level tests (open pauses; content per gym; `?`/`Close`/ESC resume; ESC does not reach the menu while open).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts` — Extend with help-button/overlay integration assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Document the gym help overlay and the catalogue `description` fields (§4.4 / §6.4).
- `README.md` — Document the `Help (?)` affordance in the gym sections.

### Risks and assumptions

- **Input routing risk (mitigated by design):** a paused Phaser scene does not receive keyboard events, so the `?`/ESC *close* handling must live in `HelpScene`; if it were left on the gym the overlay could not be dismissed by keyboard. Tests must assert resume-on-close.
- **Discovery risk (mitigated by constraint):** placing `HelpScene` in `src/scenes/gym/` would leak it into the gym index; the brief pins it to `src/scenes/` + `gameConfig.ts` registration.
- **Drift risk (mitigated by AC3):** descriptions are read from the catalogues rather than duplicated in the overlay, so a future balance change to a drop's effect forces the help text to change in one place.
- **Copy-review risk:** the proposed one-line descriptions are derived from GDD §4.4; if the producer prefers shorter/rewritten copy, only the catalogue `description` strings need editing (no structural change).
- **Scope-creep risk:** extending the help to the full-pool combat formation gyms (`GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`) and to the shipped `PlayScene` is deliberately **out of scope** for this item. If desired, record these as separate follow-up work items (`discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB67I002REOZ`) rather than growing this one. The shared helper is deliberately gym-agnostic so those follow-ups are cheap.
- **Assumption:** the dev gym index (and therefore the gyms) is only reachable in dev mode, so the overlay is a developer/QA affordance and needs no persistence or localisation.

### Related work

- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — introduces the `← INDEX` button and directory-dynamic gym discovery that the help entry point sits beside.
- **Add ESC handler to remaining direct gym scenes (AH-0MUA9BBFV004Y1T0)** — establishes the ESC-to-menu behaviour the help overlay must not break while open.
- **Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT)** — the `GymPowerUpsUtility` gym whose drops the help documents.
- **Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene (AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR)** — the `GymWeapons` gym and the weapon/reset drop set.
- **Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40)** — the `GymPowerUpsCombat` gym and the P3/P4/P6/P7 drop set.
- **Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9) (AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS)** and **Catalogue extension: P3, P4, P6, P7 entries (AH-0MTE8EB36003YF0S)** — the catalogues that gain the `description` field.
- **In-game menu (AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292)** — the `PauseScene` + `FocusManager` overlay pattern the help overlay should mirror.
- **Docs: GymPowerUps scene + ui/HUD.ts in GDD & README (AH-0MTCO0R4D0043TDL)** — the documentation surfaces to update.

### Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (scope of gym scenes).** Which scenes get the help overlay? — **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — shared, gym-agnostic helper + `HelpScene`, wired into the three named gyms only (`GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymWeapons`). Source: interactive reply to the intake agent, 2026-09-23.
- **Q2 (open/close and pause semantics).** How does help open/close and what does ESC do while it is open? — **Answer (Producer):** **A** — `?` or the `Help (?)` button opens and pauses the gym; `?` / `Close` / ESC closes and resumes; while help is open ESC closes help first and never exits to the menu. Source: interactive reply to the intake agent, 2026-09-23.
- **Q3 (content source of truth and entries).** Where do descriptions live and what does each list include? — **Answer (Producer):** **A** — add a `description` field to `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` and the weapon catalogue (plus a reset entry), render help from the catalogues; `GymWeapons` lists Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset plus the permanent Cannon. Source: interactive reply to the intake agent, 2026-09-23.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ** – Scheme-aware input tests for affected gym scenes (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G** – One Tank changes colour (completed)
- **AH-0MUD9R2OG009RA8N** – Extract input, teleport, explosion and bullet-clear into CombatScene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, acceptance, actually, add, addbacktoindexbutton (+340 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mtc2p6g3007pj40, absorbs, ac3, add, added (+331 more)

# Enemy design UI covers Gym scene buttons (AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF)

## Headline

Gym editor/control panels are anchored to the top-left of the viewport and cover
the in-scene HUD labels (lives, power-ups, minerals). All gym panels should be
re-anchored to the bottom-left so the HUD stays visible.

## Problem statement

Every gym scene that exposes a plain-DOM tuning panel positions it at
`top: 8px; left: 8px` (`#gym-config-panel`) or `top: 8px; left: 260px`
(`#enemy-gym-panel`). The Phaser HUD renders its lives / power-up / weapon /
mineral rows at the top-left of the canvas (`HUD` is constructed at `(8, 8)`),
so the panel overlays the labels a designer is actively trying to read and tune
against. The original report called these "buttons"; the operator corrected this
to the lives/power-up labels.

## Users

- **Game designer / developer** tuning ship, enemy and boss configs in the gym
  scenes, who needs the live HUD (lives, active power-ups, weapons, minerals)
  visible while the tuning panel is open.
- **QA / playtester** verifying gym scenes, who needs both the HUD and the panel
  controls usable simultaneously.

### User stories

- As a designer tuning an enemy in the gym, I want the editor panel out of the
  way of the HUD so I can see lives/power-ups change as I tune.
- As a tester opening the Player gym, I want the tuning panel anchored
  consistently (bottom-left) across every gym scene.

## Acceptance criteria

- All gym panels are anchored to the **bottom-left** of the viewport instead of the top: `#gym-config-panel` (Player), `#enemy-gym-panel` (Enemies) and `#boss-gym-panel` (Boss), sharing consistent placement rules.
- Every panel has a `max-height` bounded to the viewport (minus a reserve) with internal vertical scrolling (`overflow-y: auto`), so a tall panel never extends above the viewport or re-covers the top-left HUD.
- With a panel open, the top-left HUD labels (lives / power-ups / weapons / minerals) are fully visible and unobscured.
- The in-canvas controls (`EXPLODE`, `SHOOT`, and the Boss `DAMAGE` button) and the status line are **repositioned to the bottom-right** so they remain visible and interactive while the panel occupies the bottom-left; the hint line stays clear of the panel.
- The Boss panel (`boss-gym-panel`, currently without any positioning CSS) receives the same bottom-left anchoring / `max-height` styling as the other panels.
- Automated tests assert the panels' bottom-left anchoring (e.g. via a shared CSS class/rule or computed style), the `max-height`/scroll constraint, and the bottom-right control repositioning; testing/validation criterion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.5 and any Game Design Document references to the gym panel).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The game canvas is a fixed `960 × 540` design surface rendered with
  `Phaser.Scale.FIT`; DOM panels are `position: fixed`, in CSS pixels, and do
  **not** scale with the canvas.
- Panels are plain DOM appended to `#game-container`; each scene removes its
  panel on `SHUTDOWN` and clears stale panels on rebuild (test isolation).
- happy-dom (the test environment) performs no real layout, so tests cannot
  assert pixel geometry — they must assert the CSS rule/class or the intended
  inline style.
- No behavioural/API changes to panel contents; this is a presentation fix.
- The boss panel currently has class `gym-panel` but no CSS rule for it — this
  is a pre-existing gap to fold into the fix.

## Existing state

- `src/style.css`:
  - `#gym-config-panel { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 8px; ... }`
  - `#enemy-gym-panel { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 260px; ... }`
  - No rule for `#boss-gym-panel` or `.gym-panel`.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — standalone HUD constructed at `(8, 8)` (top-left), depth
  `HUD_DEPTH` (1000).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — builds `#gym-config-panel`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — builds `#enemy-gym-panel` (~21 rows).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — builds `#boss-gym-panel` (spawn-interval control).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — places `EXPLODE` at `(10, 480)`,
  `SHOOT` at `(120, 480)`, status text at `(10, 504)`; creates the HUD.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — adds `DAMAGE` at `(240, 480)`.

## Desired change

Re-anchor every gym panel to the bottom-left of the viewport (shared class or
per-id rules), capped with a viewport-relative `max-height` and internal
scrolling so tall panels stay on-screen below the HUD. Apply consistent styling
to the currently-unstyled boss panel. Move the in-canvas `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT`/
`DAMAGE` controls and the status line to the bottom-right so they remain usable
alongside the panel. Update documentation and add regression tests for the
anchoring and control placement.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/style.css` — Move panel anchoring from `top` to `bottom`; add a shared
  `.gym-panel` rule (and/or `#boss-gym-panel`) so all panels share bottom-left
  placement plus a viewport-relative `max-height` with `overflow-y: auto`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — apply the shared panel class/id consistently
  (already sets `className = 'gym-panel'`); move the `DAMAGE` button to the
  bottom-right.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — reposition the in-canvas
  `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT` buttons and status line to the bottom-right; keep the hint
  line clear of the panel.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — update §8.5 panel surface notes and
  the HUD-controls description (§ around line 156).
- Test files (e.g. `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`, `GymPlayer.test.ts`,
  `GymBoss.test.ts`, or a new `src/style.test.ts`) — assert bottom-left
  anchoring, the `max-height`/scroll constraint, and the bottom-right control
  coordinates.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ** – Create E3 Tank gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (open)
- **AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ** – Scheme-aware input tests for affected gym scenes (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `README.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§8.5 Gym surface — GymEnemies + editor panel)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** bottom-left is free of HUD elements — the HUD is top-left, so
  this holds.
- **Risk:** the enemy editor panel is taller than the 540 px viewport; mitigated
  by the agreed `max-height` + `overflow-y: auto` (AC2).
- **Risk:** bottom-left is occupied by the in-canvas `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT`/`DAMAGE`
  controls; mitigated by the agreed bottom-right repositioning (AC4).
- **Risk:** bottom-right placement must not collide with the top-right
  `← INDEX` button or the centred hint line; verify when repositioning.
- **Risk:** happy-dom cannot verify real overlap; mitigation is to assert the
  anchoring rule/class and the control coordinates explicitly, and document the
  visual expectation for manual verification.
- **Scope-creep risk:** reworking panel layout/compaction beyond a height cap is
  a larger design task; record as a separate work item rather than folding into
  this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which UI element is actually being covered — which buttons?
  **A (operator, interactive):** "Buttons is the wrong word, it's actually the
  lives/powerup etc. labels." — i.e. the top-left HUD labels.
- **Q:** Does this affect only the Enemy gym scene or all gym scenes with a panel?
  **A (operator, interactive):** "all scenes with a panel (player too, for

# Reduce Volume of Player Thrusters — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

Player thruster hum is too loud. The maximum gain (`THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME`) of `0.15` should be reduced by 50% to `0.075` so the thruster sound sits more comfortably in the mix without drowning out other cues.

## Users

- Player experiencing the game, hearing the thruster hum alongside other SFX (shoot, pickup, enemies, music).

## User Stories

- As a player, I hear the thruster hum at roughly half its current loudness, so it doesn't overpower other game audio.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Halved volume ceiling:** `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` in `src/audio/effects.ts` is changed from `0.15` to `0.075`. All thruster hum output is now at most 50% of its former level.
- **AC2 — GDD §7.3 updated:** The Game Design Document's Player Audio Character table and thruster hum description are updated to reflect the new `≤ 0.075` volume ceiling.
- **AC3 — No behavioural regressions:** Thruster gain envelope, rise/decay timing, detune drift, noise filtering, and all other thruster characteristics remain unchanged — only the maximum volume target is halved.
- **AC4 — Tests updated:** Any existing tests asserting `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME === 0.15` are updated to expect `0.075`. Full project test suite passes with no regressions.

## Constraints

- 50% reduction only — no other audio parameters change.
- Must not affect other SFX (shoot, pickup, enemy audio, master SFX volume).
- Procedural audio only — no external assets.

## Existing State

- `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME = 0.15` in `src/audio/effects.ts` (line 42).
- GDD §7.3 documents thruster hum at `≤ 0.15`.
- All thruster hum paths multiply their gain target by `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` (e.g. `updateThrusterSound` line: `const targetGain = clamped * THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME`).
- `effects.test.ts` asserts against `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME`.

## Desired Change

- Update `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` from `0.15` to `0.075`.
- Update GDD §7.3 to reflect the new volume ceiling.
- Update any test assertions referencing the old value.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Change `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` from `0.15` to `0.075`
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Update assertions expecting `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` (existing references use the constant, so may auto-adjust)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §7.3 thruster hum entry: change `≤ 0.15` to `≤ 0.075`

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620** — Player thruster SFX (original thruster hum implementation)
- **AH-0MTK9ZSOX009SB1K** — Thruster hum: jet-engine roar — remove buzzy sawtooth
- **AH-0MUA8B6MT006M1KS** — SFX master volume + mute plumbing in effects.ts

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Minimal change risk:** This is a single-constant change in the code path; regressions are unlikely.
- **Perceptual quality:** The hum is quieter but should still be audible — at `0.075` it remains within the `≤ 0.2` player-cue ceiling and is proportional to other player cues.
- **Test auto-adjustment:** Tests reference `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` as a constant, so most should automatically pick up the new value; spot-check for hard-coded `0.15` assertions.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Adjustments to other SFX volumes, music levels, or EQ changes are out of scope — track as `discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB8S50029QB8` work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- Q1 — Volume reduction target: "Reduce volume by 50%" — Answer: Halve `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` from `0.15` to `0.075`. Source: operator confirmation.
- Q2 — GDD update: Should §7.3 be updated? — Answer: Yes, to `≤ 0.075`. Source: operator confirmation.
- Q3 — Audio assets: External files needed? — Answer: No, procedural audio only. Source: operator confirmation.

# Intake Brief: Divers should not return (AH-0MUAYB957002EMYV)

## Headline

While a Diver is away from the formation on its dive attack, the whole enemy cluster must hold its current position (freeze its drift) and resume only once every Diver has rejoined; the Diver still returns, but to its slot in the *current* formation and never to the stale dive-start point.

## Problem statement

Divers dive out of formation toward the player, pause, then glide back to a formation that has kept drifting in the meantime. This reads as the Diver "chasing" a moving cluster and makes the return feel disconnected from the attack. The cluster should instead stop moving while a Diver is away, so the attack reads as: the formation holds, the Diver dives, pauses and rejoins the same (stationary) formation, and only then does the cluster continue on its way.

## Users

- **Player:** Reads the dive attack as deliberate — the formation hesitates, the Diver commits, and the Diver visibly re-forms with its group rather than chasing it.
- **Developer:** Gets a small, explicit "hold the formation" seam shared by the gym base scene and `PlayScene`, with deterministic tests.

Example user stories:

- *As a player, when a Diver dives at me the rest of its cluster stays put until the Diver has rejoined, so I can read where the formation is and plan my movement.*
- *As a developer, I want a single optional entity seam that tells a formation scene "hold the cluster this frame", so the gym and the shipped game cannot diverge.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — The formation holds while a Diver is away.** While any Diver is in a non-`FORMATION` state (`DIVING`, `PAUSING` or `RETURNING`), the formation base does not advance: `GymFormationScene.tick()` leaves `formationBaseX` unchanged (and does not fire the wrap/respawn), and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` leaves `driftX`/`driftDir` unchanged. *Verification:* deterministic tests in `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` assert the base/drift is unchanged after ticks with a Diver in each non-formation state, and unchanged while a second Diver is still holding; a destroyed Diver (`alive === false`) in a non-`FORMATION` state must NOT hold the formation, so the gate must consider only living entities and a mid-dive kill cannot freeze the cluster forever.
2. **AC2 — The formation resumes once every Diver has rejoined.** As soon as no Diver is detached (all in `FORMATION`), the formation resumes moving from the frozen position with no jump/snap. *Verification:* a two-diver test asserts the formation stays frozen while one is away and continues from exactly the held `formationBaseX`/`driftX` once both are back.
3. **AC3 — Divers return to their slot in the current formation.** `Diver._handleReturn()` continues to glide onto the slot evaluated live from the formation base (`baseX + col * spacingX`, `baseY + row * spacingY`) and never to a stale dive-start coordinate; a returning Diver never relocates the cluster to meet it. *Verification:* a unit test asserts the return target re-evaluates the supplied base each frame; the existing smooth-return / no-jump tests (`AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD`, `AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB`) stay green.
4. **AC4 — Dive/return geometry and existing behaviour preserved.** The diagonal bezier dive toward the snapshotted player position, the 500 ms pause, the ~3 s hold, spread-shot firing, dive/pause/return rotation, audio and explosion behaviour are all unchanged, and non-Diver entities (Scout/Tank/Phaser/Swarm/Asteroid/Boss) behave exactly as before. *Verification:* the existing `Diver.test.ts` suites pass unmodified, and a scene test confirms a formation with no Diver still drifts.
5. **AC5 — Tests, docs and full suite.** New deterministic tests cover the hold seam and freeze/resume in both scenes; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and GDD §4.1 E2); the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared seam, both scenes.** Add an optional entity method (working name `requiresFormationHold?(): boolean`) to `FormationSceneEntity` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) **and** to the shared `EnemyEntity` seam in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` (alongside `DestructionAudioSeam`), so `PlayScene` can query it on the union type. Non-Diver entities omit it; call sites use optional chaining.
- **Two drift implementations must both be gated.** `GymFormationScene.tick()` (`formationBaseX`, rightward drift + wrap) and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` (`driftX`/`driftDir`, ping-pong drift) are independent and must each consult the seam.
- **Keep the diagonal dive (Q3-A).** Do not change the dive shape, and do not fold in the open docs item `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` (GDD calls the dive vertical while the code is diagonal) — that stays a separate item.
- **No new audio/VFX and no timing/config-default changes.** Use the existing `DIVER_*` constants.
- **Freeze scope.** The hold applies for the entire detached window (`DIVING`, `PAUSING`, `RETURNING`); the formation must not wrap/respawn during a hold.
- **Out of scope:** closing formation gaps / restructuring the cluster's internal layout (`Q2-C`) and preventing wrap-only relocation (`Q2-D`) were not selected.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` runs a four-state machine (`FORMATION → DIVING → PAUSING → RETURNING → FORMATION`). The dive is a diagonal quadratic bezier from the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start (`AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX`); the pause is 500 ms (`AH-0MU0EIDQQ003S1JT`); `_handleReturn()` glides from the dive target onto the slot evaluated each frame from the live `baseX`/`baseY` (`AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB`), so it already rejoins the drifting cluster without a snap.
- The formation base is advanced unconditionally: `GymFormationScene.tick()` does `formationBaseX += config.driftSpeed * dt` then wraps when it exceeds `GAME_WIDTH + 60`; `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` advances `driftX` with a `driftDir` ping-pong bounded by `FORMATION_DRIFT_RANGE`. Neither consults entity state.
- There is no seam today by which an entity can ask its scene to hold the formation.
- Open `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` records that GDD §4.1 still describes a vertical/x-locked dive while the implementation is diagonal (pre-existing, not caused by this item).

## Desired change

1. Give the `Diver` a way to report that it is detached from the formation (working name `requiresFormationHold()` returning `this._state !== DiverState.FORMATION`), published through the shared entity seam so both scenes can query it.
2. Gate the drift advance (and, in the gym scene, the wrap/respawn) on **no** entity requiring a hold. While held, the base stays fixed; every entity's `applyFormationPosition` still runs each frame with the unchanged base so the Diver can rejoin precisely.
3. Resume normal drift automatically on the first frame after the last detached Diver re-enters `FORMATION`.
4. **Hold only on living entities.** The two scene gates must ignore destroyed Divers: a Diver killed mid-`DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING` must stop holding immediately so a dead Diver can never freeze the cluster. Implement the seam as `this.alive && this._state !== DiverState.FORMATION` (or filter `entity.alive` at both call sites) and cover it with a test.

Implementation order (test-first): (1) add the failing tests — the seam unit test in `Diver.test.ts` and the freeze/resume scene tests (single diver, two divers, destroyed diver, and no-Diver-still-drifts); (2) add the optional seam to `Diver` and to both entity interfaces (`FormationSceneEntity`, `EnemyEntity`); (3) gate the two drift sites; (4) run the full suite and update the docs (AC5).

No change is required to the Diver's return target logic — with the cluster frozen, the "current" slot is stationary, so the Diver lands exactly where it left.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — implement the `requiresFormationHold()` seam (true for `DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING`); class JSDoc note on the hold behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — add the optional seam to `FormationSceneEntity`; gate the `formationBaseX` advance + respawn in `tick()` on no entity holding.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — gate `driftX`/`driftDir` advance in `_moveEnemies()` on no entity holding.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — extend the shared `EnemyEntity` seam with the optional `requiresFormationHold` method.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — seam unit tests (state → hold true/false across the cycle).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — freeze/resume integration tests (single and multiple divers; non-Diver formation still drifts; respawn suppressed during a hold).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `_moveEnemies` freeze/resume test (ping-pong drift preserved).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document the formation hold and update the E2/behaviour tables.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — GDD §4.1 E2: note that the cluster holds while a Diver is away.

## Related work

- `AH-0MU0EIDQQ003S1JT` — *Diver should pause before returning* (completed): introduced `DiverState.PAUSING` with a configurable 500 ms pause. This item extends the attack window that now holds the formation.
- `AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB` — *Fix Diver.ts: lock x during dive and smooth return to current formation slot* (completed) and `AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD` — *Diver jumps on return from dive* (completed): established the smooth return onto the *current* slot, which AC3 preserves.
- `AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX` — *Diver should rotate to face the player and dive towards them* (completed): made the dive diagonal and player-targeted; preserved by AC4/Q3-A.
- `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` — *Diver docs stale: dive described as x-locked but implemented as diagonal* (open): related documentation discrepancy, explicitly **not** folded into this item.
- `AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW` — *GymDiver AC1 … wall-clock flaky under full-suite parallel load* (completed): determinism precedent for the new tests (tick-driven, no wall-clock).
- `AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4` — *Stale formation entities crash on GymEnemies scene restart* (completed): the `_localPhase`/no-`scene`-deref constraint that the seam must respect (no new `scene` dereference in the Diver).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (documented, Q2-B):** `PAUSING` counts as "away", so the freeze covers all non-`FORMATION` states. This keeps the cluster stationary for the entire attack rather than twitching during the 500 ms pause.
- **Risk — long freezes when divers are desynchronised.** All divers share the same hold timer, so they normally dive together and the cluster freezes for the attack window (~3.3 s of a ~6.3 s cycle). If divers become desynchronised (destruction and later respawn), the cluster could be held for extended periods. Mitigation: the hold is released as soon as no diver is detached; monitor during playtest and tune the hold timing if it reads poorly.
- **Risk — ping-pong drift state.** In `PlayScene` the freeze must not corrupt `driftDir`; the resume test must assert direction continuity.
- **Risk — destroyed divers.** A Diver destroyed mid-dive/return must stop holding the formation (its `alive` flag is false / it is removed). Add a test so a dead Diver cannot freeze the cluster forever.
- **Assumption:** non-Diver formations and asteroid roaming are unaffected; the seam is optional and only the Diver implements it.
- **Scope-creep risk:** gap-closing/restructuring (`Q2-C`) and wrap-only relocation (`Q2-D`) were offered and not selected; any such ideas should be recorded as linked work items rather than added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

The seed description was ambiguous, so the Diver behaviour was confirmed by the producer before the brief was finalised.

- **Q1 — Does "Divers should not return" mean they must not return at all, or that they must not return to the stale start point?** — **Answer (producer): "1. a" → they still return, but to their slot in the *current* formation, never to the dive-start point.** Source: interactive reply. Consequence: AC3; no state-machine removal of the return.
- **Q2 — What does "the cluster of enemies should not move from their current location other than to restructure the formation" require in practice?** — **Answer (producer): "2. b" → freeze the whole formation's drift while any Diver is diving/returning; resume once every Diver has rejoined.** Source: interactive reply. Consequence: AC1, AC2; both `GymFormationScene` and `PlayScene` drifts are gated. `Q2-C` (gap-closing) and `Q2-D` (wrap-only relocation) rejected.
- **Q3 — Is the dive/return geometry in scope?** — **Answer (producer): "3. a" → keep the current diagonal dive and the straight glide from the dive target to the current slot; scope this item to *where the Diver rejoins*.** Source: interactive reply. Consequence: AC4; `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` stays separate.
- Research note: the questions and the current-behaviour evidence were recorded on the work item in comment `AH-C0MUIFH7OK004J7RP` while the item was flagged `needsProducerReview`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTECNI8K008FSKH** – Implement: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MG91005XHA8** – Tests: Config store (in-memory registry, boot load, dev write) (completed)
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** – Enemy Design tooling (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, add (+293 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+290 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac4, add, added, advance (+271 more)

# Speed Power Up Should Increase All Speeds

## Problem statement

The P5 Speed Boost power-up currently increases only the player ship's movement speed (thrust and max-speed) by 50 %. It does **not** affect rate of fire, so an active Speed Boost does not deliver the intended "all speeds" boost. This change extends P5 so it increases the player's rate of fire as well as their movement speed, and updates the GDD and related descriptions to match.

## Users

- **Player** — when collecting a Speed Boost (P5), expects both faster movement and faster firing for the 10-second duration.
  - *"As a player, when I collect a Speed Boost (P5) I expect to move 50 % faster **and** fire 50 % faster for 10 seconds."*
- **Game designer / producer** — expects the Game Design Document to describe P5 accurately as affecting all speeds.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — With P5 active, the player's **rate of fire increases by 50 %** (effective fire interval `fireRateMs` is scaled by `1 / 1.5`, i.e. the ship fires 1.5 × as often) in the playable game (`PlayScene`).
- **AC2** — The fire-rate multiplier is applied **live every frame** and returns to 1 immediately when P5 expires; re-collecting P5 refreshes the full 10 s duration (never additive); an active P5 continues to apply through a respawn.
- **AC3** — Movement speed and rate of fire derive from a **single source of truth** in `EffectsRegistry` (one P5 multiplier value of 1.5), and P5's duration, multiplier value and registry semantics are otherwise unchanged.
- **AC4** — **Gym parity:** every gym scene that can obtain P5 applies the same P5 multipliers as the game — `GymPowerUpsUtility` (round-robin P5 drop) and the shared `GymFormationScene` (P5 via the hold-full choice, inherited by the combat gyms). This includes applying the **movement** multiplier wherever it is currently missing, so gyms remain the parity reference for both speeds.
- **AC5** — **Unit tests** cover: P5 active → effective fire rate boosted / cooldown scaled; P5 expired → fire rate back to normal; re-collect refreshes duration; multiplier is non-additive and survives respawn.
- **AC6** — **Documentation updated:** the GDD P5 entry states that the Speed Boost increases movement speed **and** rate of fire by 50 % for 10 s; module doc comments (`effects.ts`, `types.ts`), power-up `description` strings and README references are updated to match. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship skill release pipeline.)
- **AC7** — **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- P5 duration (10 s) and multiplier value (1.5 ×) must not change; the registry remains the single authority for the multiplier.
- The registry module must stay engine-agnostic (no Phaser imports).
- Gyms must always match the game (producer-confirmed principle) — do not implement the game change without the matching gym change.
- GDD is currently the only spec that describes P5; it must be updated as part of this work (no separate spec to change).

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` (src/powerups/effects.ts) returns `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER` (1.5) while P5 is active, else 1. It is the single authority for P5.
- `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (src/entities/Player.ts) scales `thrust` and `maxSpeed` about the base config; friction is untouched.
- `Player.tryFire(dt)` (src/entities/Player.ts) advances per-weapon cooldowns using the raw `getWeaponById(weaponId).fireRateMs` — **no multiplier is applied**.
- `CombatScene._autoFire(dt)` (src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts) calls `player.tryFire(dt)` and spawns bullets for the returned weapon ids.
- `PlayScene` tick applies `player.setSpeedMultiplier(this.effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier())` but nothing for fire rate.
- `GymPowerUpsUtility` applies `setSpeedMultiplier(...)` each frame but no fire-rate multiplier.
- GDD §4.4 (docs/Game Design Document.md) P5 row: *"Increases movement speed by 50 % for 10 seconds"* — movement only.

## Desired change

1. Add a P5 fire-rate multiplier accessor to `EffectsRegistry` (e.g. `fireRateMultiplier()` returning `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER` while active, else 1). Keep a single constant so movement and fire rate cannot diverge.
2. Extend `Player` to accept and apply a live fire-rate multiplier in `tryFire(dt)` (scale the effective interval/cooldown), mirroring `setSpeedMultiplier` and re-applied every frame.
3. Wire the multiplier into `PlayScene` tick alongside the existing speed-multiplier application, and into the gym scene(s) that collect P5.
4. Update the GDD P5 entry, `effects.ts` / `types.ts` doc comments, power-up `description` strings and README references.
5. Add unit tests at the registry, `Player` and scene levels.

**Assumption (documented, producer-confirmed direction):** "increase rate of fire by 50 %" is interpreted as an effective **1.5 × fire rate** — the fire interval is divided by 1.5 (`fireRateMs / 1.5`), so the ship fires 50 % more often per unit time. This matches the movement multiplier so "all speeds" scale identically.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Add `fireRateMultiplier()` (or equivalent) returning the P5 multiplier; update P5 doc comment.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Update P5 `description` string to mention rate of fire.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Add live fire-rate multiplier state + application in `tryFire()`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Apply the fire-rate multiplier each tick (alongside `setSpeedMultiplier`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — Apply the fire-rate multiplier each tick (gym parity).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Apply the P5 movement + fire-rate multipliers (P5 reachable via the hold-full choice); closes the pre-existing movement-parity gap.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Possibly route the multiplier through `_autoFire` if the Player API is not the chosen seam.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update P5 row/description.
- `README.md` — Update power-up summary reference if it mentions P5 movement-only.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8QURXB008DWM7** — "PlayScene: apply P5 Speed Boost multiplier live" (completed, shipped v0.1.4). Added the movement-speed application to PlayScene; **rate of fire was explicitly not included**, which is the gap this item closes.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — "Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md" (discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB). Verification found the gym-parity rule is **not** stated in the repo-local `AGENTS.md`; this follow-up adds it.
- Parent epic context: AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M (Playable game fine-tuning, if applicable).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** "all speeds" could be read to include bullet speed, enemy drift, etc. Scope is bounded to **player movement speed + player rate of fire** only; anything wider becomes a linked follow-up work item, not scope here.
- **Interpretation risk:** multiplying rate vs dividing interval. Mitigation: document the 1.5 ×-rate interpretation explicitly (above) and cover it with a test asserting the effective cooldown.
- **Gym divergence risk:** if the multiplier is applied only in `PlayScene`, gyms drift from the game. Mitigation: AC4 + the shared registry accessor make parity mechanical.
- **Respawn interaction:** multiplier must be re-applied each frame (not cached at collect time) so it survives respawn and expiry — covered by AC2/AC5.
- **Pre-existing gym gap:** `GymFormationScene` can collect P5 (hold-full choice) but never applied the movement multiplier even before this item. AC4 folds that fix in as part of parity; if it proves non-trivial it can be split into a linked follow-up.
- **Assumption:** no dedicated balance config value is needed; P5 keeps the existing single 1.5 constant for both axes.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTAFH1ZF003EGDF** – Add ship deceleration when no inputs, with slider to control deceleration rate (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (open)
- **AH-0MU7JTEA6002GE37** – Playable game — fine-tuning and follow-up fixes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: contexthub, fire, hell, increase, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, speeds, well, work
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: fire, hell, increase, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, speeds, well, work
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: belongs, fire, hell, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, work

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Does P5 Speed Boost increase fire rate?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"Confirmed - all speeds, update documentation and descriptions."* The GDD previously described movement only; this is a confirmed design change, and docs/descriptions are to be updated. Source: interactive reply in session.
- **Q2: By what factor?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"Yes"* confirming the same 50 % (1.5 ×) factor as movement speed. Source: interactive reply in session.
- **Q3: Should gym scenes match the game? Is the gym-parity principle clear in the repo-local AGENTS.md?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"yes - gym scenes should always match the game. This should be clear in the local AGENTS.md - verify it is clear."* Research: `grep -ni 'gym\|parity\|reference' AGENTS.md` found **no** gym-parity guidance, so the principle is **not** clear. This item therefore applies the parity requirement directly in AC4.
