# implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to remote dev

## Headline

After `implement.py finish <child>` pushes the child's branch to `origin/dev`, the
main checkout's local `dev` branch is left one or more commits behind, so the next
`implement.py parent <epic>` / `implement.py start <child>` creates the following
child's worktree from a stale base and is missing the previous sibling's files.

> **Repo note (important):** the defect is in **agent infrastructure** that lives in
> the **SorraAgents** repository, not in AI_Hell — `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
> (the global skill at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` is a symlink to
> `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement`). AI_Hell contains no
> `implement.py`. This AI_Hell item is therefore the **discovery report**; the fix and
> its regression tests are tracked in the SorraAgents counterpart
> **`SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1`** with tag `discovered-from:AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB`. This mirrors
> the established precedent `SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V` (`discovered-from:AH-0MT94ULUU001NBW3`).

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` restores the main checkout to the parent branch **before** pushing the
just-committed branch to `origin dev`:

- Step 7 — `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` runs `git checkout dev` then
  `git pull origin dev` (i.e. local `dev` is fast-forwarded to the **pre-push** remote tip).
- Step 8 — `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch)` runs
  `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` (the new commit lands on the remote *after* the pull).

The result is that local `dev` is left exactly one (or more) commits behind
`origin/dev`. `git_worktree_add()` then forks each child from the **local** parent branch
(`git worktree add --track -b <branch> <worktree> dev`), and `phase_start` performs no fetch,
so every subsequent child starts from the stale base.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running the parent/epic flow (`implement.py parent`).
- **Operators / orchestrators** relying on the parent flow to be self-consistent without
  manual `git fetch` / `git merge` steps.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, after `finish` reports "commit pushed to dev", I want the
  main checkout's local `dev` to contain that commit, so that the next `parent`/`start`
  child worktree includes my just-finished sibling's files.
- As an operator, I want the parent flow to never create a child from a stale base, so I
  do not have to diagnose phantom build errors (e.g. unresolved imports) or risk
  lost/duplicated work.

## Observed (evidence)

- F2 (`AH-0MUBYU600004YU4T`) `finish` pushed commit `91538d0` to `origin/dev`; local `dev`
  stayed at `1920e65`.
- The F3 worktree (`AH-0MUBYXR280018HST`) was created from local `dev` `1920e65` and could
  not resolve `../powerups/collectAnimation` (added by F2) until local `dev` was manually
  fast-forwarded to `origin/dev` and merged into the worktree.
- Workaround was applied by hand during the parent `AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W` run.

## Impact

Every child after the first can be created from a stale base. This causes phantom build
errors, wasted agent cycles, and risks lost or duplicated work when a sibling's changes are
invisible to the next child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Post-push local parent sync.** After a successful push in `phase_finish`, the
  main checkout's local parent branch (`dev`) is at least as advanced as the tip that was
  pushed (i.e. local `dev` == pushed commit == `origin/dev`) when it is safe to
  fast-forward. Measurable: a regression test asserts the local branch ref equals the
  pushed commit after a successful `finish`.
- [ ] **AC2 — Safe-skip semantics.** When it is **not** safe to update (main checkout dirty,
  checkout on another branch/detached, or local `dev` diverged), `finish` must not force the
  update, must not lose local commits, and must not fail the finish phase. The skipped
  update is reported (log/step result/comment) and leaves the repo recoverable. Measurable:
  tests cover a dirty main checkout and a diverged local `dev`; both finish successfully with
  local commits intact.
- [ ] **AC3 — Children never start from a stale base.** `implement.py parent` / `start`
  create each child worktree from an up-to-date base: the parent branch is refreshed
  (`git fetch origin <parent_branch>` + fast-forward) before `git worktree add`, **or** the
  worktree is created from `origin/<parent_branch>` after a fetch. Measurable: a test starts
  a child after a sibling's commit is pushed and asserts the child worktree contains the
  sibling's file/commit.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression test suite.** A focused regression test (e.g.
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`) covers AC1, AC2 and AC3; the
  existing implement tests (`tests/test_implement_*.py`) all still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite passes.** Full project test suite must pass with the
  new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, README, and any relevant docs-site
  entries.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary:** the fix must be made in the SorraAgents repo
  (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, tests under `tests/`). Do **not** edit
  agent-infrastructure from the AI_Hell checkout.
- No new runtime dependencies; use stdlib and the existing `run_cmd` / `git_*` helpers.
- Must be **safe**: never force-update a branch with local commits; prefer `--ff-only`.
- Must not regress worktree-based finish (finish may run from inside the worktree, and the
  worktree is removed before the push).
- Must not introduce a fetch/pull on a path that today has none if that would break
  `--no-refactor`/offline runs — the update should degrade gracefully when the remote is
  unreachable (report, do not fail the successfully-pushed finish).
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_PARENT_BRANCH = "dev"`.
- `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` → `git checkout dev`; `git pull origin dev` (no
  `--ff-only`, no error handling on failure).
- `git_push_to_dev(cwd, branch)` → `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev`.
- `git_worktree_add(branch, worktree_path, parent_branch)` →
  `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <worktree> <parent_branch>`; `phase_start` does no
  fetch and does not resolve `origin/<parent_branch>`.
- `phase_finish` call order: Step 6 remove worktree → Step 7 `_restore_repo_state` →
  Step 8 `git_push_to_dev`.

## Desired change

1. **Post-push local parent sync (AC1/AC2).** After a *successful* push, fast-forward the
   main checkout's local parent branch to the pushed tip when safe. Simplest correct change:
   move the parent-branch restore (`checkout` + `pull --ff-only`) to **after** the push (or
   add an explicit post-push `git fetch origin <parent>` + `git merge --ff-only
   origin/<parent>`), guarded so a dirty/diverged/other-branch main checkout is skipped with
   a clear report rather than a failure.
2. **Fresh worktree base (AC3).** In `phase_start` (or `git_worktree_add`), fetch the parent
   branch and fork the worktree from the refreshed local branch (or `origin/<parent_branch>`)
   so children never start stale even when another actor pushed.
3. **Tests (AC4/AC5).** Add a focused regression test using the existing hermetic git
   sandbox/fixtures; extend `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py` /
   `test_implement_parent_safety.py` where the parent flow is exercised.
4. **Docs (AC6).** Document the post-push local parent sync (and the safety skip) in
   `skill/implement/SKILL.md` if the behaviour is described there.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — reorder the `_restore_repo_state` / `git_push_to_dev`
  steps in `phase_finish`, add a guarded `--ff-only` post-push sync helper, and refresh the
  parent branch in `phase_start` before `git_worktree_add`.
- `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` — new regression test for AC1–AC3.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` —
  extend the parent-flow coverage (fresh base for the next child).
- `tests/conftest.py` / hermetic git sandbox helper — reuse the existing hermetic sandbox
  (do not touch the live SorraAgents checkout).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the post-push local parent sync behaviour and the
  safe-skip semantics.

## Related work

### Related work items

- **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1** — *implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to
  remote dev* (open, SorraAgents): the actionable counterpart created by this intake that
  carries the fix and regression tests (`discovered-from:AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB`).
- **AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W** — *Collected powerups need some feel* (completed): the parent epic
  during whose run the stale-base problem was observed and worked around.
- **SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V** — *Audit merge gate hard-codes npm run build…* (open): precedent for
  the AI_Hell report → SorraAgents counterpart pattern (`discovered-from:AH-0MT94ULUU001NBW3`).
- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** — *Implement skill safety gate should account for git worktrees*
  (completed): prior work making the implement flow worktree-aware.
- **SA-0MSIVM00X003E5PZ** — *implement.py finish aborts on npm run build for repos with no
  build script* (completed); **SA-0MSI8YLTN0007KN8** — *implement.py finish hardcodes npm run
  build…* (completed): other `phase_finish` robustness fixes.
- **SA-0MQJIL0HN0053Q4M** — *Implement: remove push-to-dev from implement* (completed, docs
  only): relevant to whether `finish` should push to `dev` at all; current
  `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `implement.py` still push, so the sync fix applies to the
  current behaviour.

### Repository file matches

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_restore_repo_state`, `git_push_to_dev`,
  `git_worktree_add`, `phase_finish`, `phase_start`.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — describes the push-to-dev step and worktree lifecycle.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py` — existing implement-flow tests/fixtures.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (ownership):** the fix belongs to the SorraAgents repo. Evidence: the code
  lives there; AI_Hell has no `implement.py`; the global skill is a symlink into SorraAgents;
  the counterpart pattern is established (`SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V`).
- **Assumption (scope):** the defect is the **ordering** of restore-vs-push plus the absence
  of a fetch in `phase_start`; both are addressed so AC3 holds even with concurrent actors.
- **Risk:** auto-updating local `dev` could clobber a user's intentional local commits —
  mitigate with a clean/on-branch/no-divergence guard and `--ff-only`.
- **Risk:** `git pull`/`fetch` in a dirty or offline main checkout — must never fail a finish
  that already pushed successfully; report and continue.
- **Risk:** extra fetch on `start` adds latency — acceptable and bounded to one fetch.
- **Risk (scope creep):** a generic "sync all worktrees" mechanism or changing the
  push-to-`dev` policy itself are out of scope; record as separate work items if wanted.
- **Risk (cross-repo drift):** the AI_Hell report and the SorraAgents counterpart could
  diverge; link both directions and keep the counterpart authoritative for implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required: the seed context plus repository/worklog research
resolved the requirements. Research-derived answers are recorded below.

- **Q: Which repository owns the fix?**
  — **Answer (agent research):** SorraAgents. Evidence: `implement.py` resolves to
  `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  (the global `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` is a symlink into SorraAgents); AI_Hell contains
  no `implement.py`; the source of truth for the skill is the SorraAgents repo. Source:
  filesystem + `readlink`.
- **Q: Is there an existing SorraAgents counterpart for this defect?**
  — **Answer (agent research):** none found. `wl search` for "implement.py",
  "local parent branch", "remote dev", "finish leaves local" returned no matching open/in-progress
  item. Source: SorraAgents worklog searches.
- **Q: How was a comparable agent-infrastructure bug reported from AI_Hell previously?**
  — **Answer (agent research):** a SorraAgents counterpart was created with tag
  `discovered-from:<AH-id>` — `SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V` for `AH-0MT94ULUU001NBW3` (created
  ~33 min after the AH report). Source: worklog metadata for both items.
- **Q: Is the bug still present?**
  — **Answer (agent research):** yes. In `phase_finish`, Step 7 `_restore_repo_state`
  (`checkout dev` + `pull origin dev`) runs before Step 8 `git_push_to_dev`. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` lines ~2649–2656.
- **Q: Should implementation proceed via the new SorraAgents counterpart (rather than
  attempting any change in AI_Hell), and was creating a cross-repo counterpart during this
  intake the expected handling?**
  — **Answer (producer):** "Implementation should be in the SorraAgents project." Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-09-25. **Resolved:** the AI_Hell item remains the discovery report;
  the fix and regression tests are implemented and tracked in
  **`SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1`** (tag `discovered-from:AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB`). No change in AI_Hell.

## Related work (automated report)

> Keyword-driven (find-related skill) against the AI_Hell worklog. It is mostly noise
> because the defect is agent infrastructure; the curated "Related work" section above is
> authoritative. Retained for traceability.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT9XNDZB003IAO1** – Remove accidentally-committed node_modules symlink from repo (completed)
- **AH-0MTFM9QX5004EMNW** – [test-failure] GymPhaser.test.ts AC3 — Phasers move in orbital paths around the formation centre — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MTCNYWDO007B6CJ** – Unit tests: power-up effects, refresh & magnet math (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, added, advanced, applied, base (+62 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: added, advanced, base, branch, build (+55 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muayb3ou0087h9w, added, applied, base, build (+45 more)

# Intake brief — Extract shared combat core into standalone gym scenes

**Headline:** Re-base the three remaining standalone gym scenes (`GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) on the shared combat core so no production scene keeps a divergent copy of the eight combat/lifecycle methods. Use a hybrid architecture: `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`, while the two threat-free gyms consume a narrower shared base that `CombatScene` also builds on.

## Problem statement

The parent epic (`AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO`) extracted the shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) and re-based `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`, deliberately leaving the three older standalone gym scenes out of scope. Those three still carry their own copies of shared method names. Because the copies are independent, a behaviour fix or feature applied to the shared core does not reach these gyms, so they can silently diverge from the shipped game and the other gyms. This item eliminates the last divergent copies.

## Users

- **Player** — expects every gym to exercise the same combat/collection code as the shipped game.
  - *As a player, I want the standalone gyms to behave the same as the shared core, so that practising in a gym reflects the real game.*
- **Developer / designer** — wants one code path to change.
  - *As a developer, when I change collection, auto-fire, teleport or hit behaviour I want to change it once, so the gyms cannot drift apart.*
- **Tester** — wants the shared seams covered in one place.
  - *As a tester, I want a repo-wide guard proving the eight methods are defined once, so future duplication is caught automatically.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Single shared definition of the eight methods.** Across all production scene files, each of `_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport` and `_readPlayerInput` is defined exactly once, in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` and/or `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`). Verified by extending the existing `definesMethod` guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` to scan every production scene file repo-wide.
- [ ] **AC2 — `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends the shared combat core.** `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene` and no longer defines `_collectDrop`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport` or `_hitPlayer`. Its shield/phase/bomb/teleport/invulnerability behaviour is supplied through hooks (`tryAbsorbPlayerHit`, `isPlayerPhased`, `onPowerUpCollected`, `getInvulnerabilityDuration`). Verified by `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` passing and a prototype-identity assertion against `CombatScene`.
- [ ] **AC3 — Threat-free gyms consume the narrower shared core.** `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` extend the narrower shared base and no longer define `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` or `_readInput`. Their per-type pickup audio and auto-fire cues are supplied through hooks (`onWeaponFired`, `_playPickupCue`/`onPowerUpCollected`). Verified by `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` passing plus prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC4 — Input path unified.** The private `_readInput` copies in all three gyms are removed; input mapping flows through the shared `_readPlayerInput` (covered by the AC1 guard and by the scene suites).
- [ ] **AC5 — Behaviour preserved, with two approved exceptions.** Existing gym suites pass, and the only observable behaviour changes are the two explicitly approved ones: (a) `GymPowerUpsCombat` keeps its 0.8 s post-hit invulnerability via a `getInvulnerabilityDuration()` hook (the shared logic refactor does not change the timing), and (b) the shared teleport activation (`S` **and** `↓`) now applies in `GymPowerUpsCombat`, fixing its `S`-only implementation to match GDD §2.3. Verified by `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` suites.
- [ ] **AC6 — Shared-core validation coverage.** The newly shared seams (auto-fire cue, drop collection/cue, input mapping, and the `getInvulnerabilityDuration` hook) are covered by base-class stub-subclass tests; cross-scene behavioural equivalence for the shared paths remains asserted by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` where relevant, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4 (Module / File Breakdown) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, describing the shared base/mixin split and the hooks the standalone gyms implement.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- **Architecture (operator decision Q1-C):** hybrid — `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`; `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` consume a narrower shared base covering drop collection + auto-fire + input, and `CombatScene` builds on that same base so there is one definition of those methods.
- **Invulnerability duration (operator decision Q2-B):** add a single overridable hook (`getInvulnerabilityDuration()`), shared default 1.5 s (game), with `GymPowerUpsCombat` overriding to 0.8 s — preserve observable timing, keep one hit-logic path.
- **Teleport activation (operator decision Q2):** adopt the shared `S`+`↓` behaviour; document as a deliberate fix of the gym's `S`-only path.
- **AC scope (operator decision Q3):** the repo-wide guard targets all eight shared method names; the private `_readInput` copies are unified onto `_readPlayerInput`. The duplicated set is 7 usages (2 + 4 + 1), not 8 — `GymPowerUpsCombat` has no `_autoFire`.
- **No full engine extraction:** spawning, wave management, HUD and menus stay scene-local; only the shared method names are consolidated.
- **Generics/type-safety:** `CombatScene` is generic (`<TEnemy, TBullet, TDrop>`); the narrower base must accommodate the same generics without weakening existing type-safety.
- **Preserve public/test seams:** `getBullets()`/`advanceBullets()` (GymWeapons), `spawnDrop()`, `getDrops()`, `getCollectAnimations()`, `getEnemyBullets()`, `triggerTeleport()`, `getPlayerHitCount()`, `isPlayerInvulnerable()` and the shared help/back-button handles must keep working.
- **Preserve semantics:** collision radii, hit radii, collection gating (≥ 3 % scale) and the power-up lifecycles must be unchanged.
- **Minimum churn:** match existing style; do not delete unrelated dead code (report it instead).

## Existing state

Confirmed by inspection (2026-09-25):

- The shared combat core exists: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` defines the eight template methods; `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` already extend it.
- The three standalone gyms still extend `Phaser.Scene` directly and define their own copies:

| File | Shared methods still defined | Line refs |
|---|---|---|
| `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` | `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` (plus private `_readInput`) | 233, 418 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` | `_collectDrop`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport`, `_hitPlayer` (plus private `_readInput`) | 423, 471, 538, 647 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` | `_collectDrop` (plus private `_readInput`) | 282 |

- The duplicate-body guard lives in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (`definesMethod()`, regex over source). It is currently scoped to the three re-based files; its own comment notes the standalone gyms "predate the shared core" and "a repo-wide scan would flag them".
- `GymWeapons` has **no** `EffectsRegistry` (the shared `_collectDrop` requires one) and keeps its own `bullets` list. `GymPowerUpsUtility` has an `EffectsRegistry`. `GymPowerUpsCombat` has an `EffectsRegistry`, a 3-scout V-formation and its own `_hitPlayer`/`_handleTeleport` with an inline shield cycle.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat` invulnerability is `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION = 0.8 s`; the shared `applyPlayerHit` uses `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE = 1.5 s`.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat._handleTeleport` computes the `↓` key state but discards it (`if (!justDown) return;`), so it is `S`-only in practice.

## Desired change

1. Introduce a narrower shared base (working name `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) owning the input path (`_readPlayerInput`, cursor/WASD/handler fields), auto-fire (`_autoFire`, `spawnPlayerBullet`, `onWeaponFired`), drop collection (`_collectDrop`, `_startCollectAnimation`, `_updateCollectAnimations`, pickup cues) and the player-explosion/collect registries. Include the new `getInvulnerabilityDuration()` hook (default 1.5 s) and the `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` hooks.
2. Refactor `CombatScene` to extend that base, keeping the combat-only template methods (`_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_handleTeleport`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`) and the enemy/bullet participant contract.
3. Re-base `GymPowerUpsCombat` on `CombatScene`: implement `getPlayer`, `getEffectsRegistry`, `getEnemyEntities` (scouts), `getEnemyBullets`/`setEnemyBullets` (scout bullets), `onPowerUpCollected` (P4 bomb notice), `tryAbsorbPlayerHit` (shield pop + short invuln), `isPlayerPhased`, `getInvulnerabilityDuration` (0.8 s) and `onEnemyDestroyed`; remove the four duplicated methods and `_readInput`; use the shared collision path instead of `_handleHits`.
4. Re-base `GymWeapons` on the narrower base: give it an `EffectsRegistry`, move its bullet list to the shared `playerBullets`, implement `onWeaponFired` (from `_playShootCue`), `onWeaponCollected`/`_playPickupCue` (per-type weapon/Reset cues) and `getBullets()`/`advanceBullets()` seams; remove `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` and `_readInput`.
5. Re-base `GymPowerUpsUtility` on the narrower base: implement `_playPickupCue`/`onPowerUpCollected` for the P5/P8/P9 cues; remove `_collectDrop` and `_readInput`.
6. Broaden the duplicate-body guard to a repo-wide scan (or extract it to a shared test helper used by both guards).
7. Update the documentation listed under AC7.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — **new**: narrower shared base (input, auto-fire, drop collection, registries, `getInvulnerabilityDuration` hook); `CombatScene` extends it.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — extend `CombatCoreScene`; keep the collision/teleport/hit template methods; remove the parts now owned by the narrower base.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts` — base stub-subclass tests for the shared seams.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — broaden the `definesMethod` guard to a repo-wide scan; adjust identity/prototype assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — extend the narrower base; hooks for cues; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`; keep public test seams.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — extend `CombatScene`; implement participant accessors and hooks; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — extend the narrower base; hook for pickup cues; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — verify behaviour preserved and public test seams unchanged.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — describe the shared base/mixin split and hooks.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — hybrid split ambiguity.** Deciding which methods belong to the narrower base vs `CombatScene` can sprawl. Mitigation: keep the narrower base to input + auto-fire + drop collection + registries; anything collision/teleport/hit-specific stays in `CombatScene`.
- **Risk — `GymWeapons` registry introduction.** Adding an `EffectsRegistry` to a scene that never had one could subtly alter collection. Mitigation: assert collection/audio behaviour with the existing `GymWeapons` suite and add hook-level tests for `onWeaponCollected`.
- **Risk — shield-absorbed invulnerability.** The shared `_hitPlayer` short-circuits on `tryAbsorbPlayerHit` without starting invulnerability, whereas `GymPowerUpsCombat` currently blinks after a shield pop. Mitigation: have the gym's `tryAbsorbPlayerHit` override start the invulnerability explicitly, and assert it.
- **Risk — collision-order change.** Replacing the gym's `_handleHits` with the shared `_handleCollisions` changes iteration/ordering. Mitigation: keep "one hit per frame" via the shared invulnerability gate, and cover bullet-then-body ordering with tests.
- **Risk — test coupling to private internals.** Both suites reach into private methods. Mitigation: keep method names/visibility on the shared base; update tests to assert hooks/shared path rather than a specific class.
- **Risk — scope creep into a full engine extraction.** Deliberately excluded; record any extra opportunity as a linked work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption (confirmed Q1):** hybrid architecture (option C).
- **Assumption (confirmed Q2):** preserve 0.8 s invulnerability via a hook; adopt shared `S`+`↓` teleport.
- **Assumption (confirmed Q3):** repo-wide eight-method guard; unify `_readInput`; corrected duplication set is 7 usages.
- **Assumption:** the repo-wide guard is broadened/extracted rather than replaced by a new script.
- **Assumption:** the narrower shared base is a class (`CombatCoreScene`), which is simpler than a true TypeScript mixin while satisfying "or a shared mixin"; naming is indicative and may change during implementation.

# Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment

## Context

This work item was discovered during planning for AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K (Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive). The Producer confirmed in Q4 that a runtime auto-sequencer is out of scope for the MVP but should be recorded as a follow-up.

discovered-from:AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K

## Relationship

This is a **non-blocking follow-up sibling** of AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K, linked via `discovered-from`. The Producer confirmed (round-3 answer, 2026-09-23) that it must NOT be a blocking child of the parent: the parent's design-time scorer deliverable is complete and the auto-sequencer is deferred future work. It was reparented to top level accordingly.

## Goal

Build a runtime system that dynamically selects and arranges enemies to hit a target difficulty curve, using the difficulty scoring primitive from the parent work item.

## Scope

- Reads the target difficulty curve from a design-time config
- Uses the enemyDifficulty() scorer from the parent work item to evaluate candidate enemy combinations
- Picks enemy groups that best fit each wave target difficulty
- Optionally adjusts counts, spacing, or formation to fine-tune

## Out of scope for now

- Player-state adaptation (adjusting difficulty based on player performance)
- A dedicated UI for tuning the difficulty curve
- Integration with the Enemy Gym editor (the scoring library is the first step)

## Delivered implementation (scope clarification)

The delivered implementation lives in `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` with tests in `src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts` (21 tests, merged to `dev` in commit `fc7158c`). It refines the original scope as follows:

- Fine-tuning is over the enemy **count** parameter only, via binary search within `[minCount, maxCount]` (clamped to `[1, 200]`). Spacing and formation are **not** adjusted; `CandidateGroup.adjustableFields` is declarative and currently only `count` is exercised.
- `shootEnabled` defaults to whether the selected archetype's `shotPattern !== 'none'`, overridable via `SequencerOptions.defaultShootEnabled`.
- Target scores use the same 0-100 scale as `enemyDifficulty()`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Curve-driven wave generation** - `sequencer(curve, candidates, options)` returns one `ShootableWave` per entry in the design-time `DifficultyCurveConfig`, with `targetDifficulty` equal to the corresponding input target, and a matching-length `errors` array.
2. **Scoring via the parent primitive** - each candidate group is evaluated using the existing `enemyDifficulty()` scorer; the sequencer selects the candidate with the smallest absolute error for each wave and records that error in `errors`.
3. **Count fine-tuning** - `adjustGroupForTarget()` tunes the enemy `count` by binary search within `[minCount, maxCount]` (clamped to `[1, 200]`), returns the best group with its achieved `score`, and stops once within `tolerance`.
4. **Default candidate pool** - `defaultCandidatePool()` returns one candidate per seed archetype (scout, diver, tank, phaser, swarm, boss, asteroid) with `count` adjustable and valid ranges (`1 <= minCount <= maxCount <= 200`).
5. **Validation and edge cases** - a candidate with `minCount > maxCount` throws a descriptive error; an empty curve yields empty `waves`/`errors`; an empty candidate pool yields an empty group per wave.
6. **Test coverage** - the sequencer behaviours above are covered by automated tests in `src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts`, and the full test suite passes at the audited HEAD.

## Key Files

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts`

# Player-death juice parameter model and constants

## Goal
Provide the pure, testable foundation for the player-death "juice": a single
`resolveJuiceParams(severity)` mapping and all tunable constants in one module
(`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), so the rendering layers and scene wiring stay thin.

## User story
As a developer/designer tuning feel, I can change shake intensity, flash alpha,
debris/shockwave counts and severity multipliers in one module, and the exported
parameter model is covered by unit tests so tuning does not silently regress.

## Scope
- New module `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` exporting:
  - `PlayerDeathSeverity = 'respawn' | 'fatal'`.
  - `interface PlayerDeathJuiceParams` (shake intensity/duration, flash
    alpha/duration/colour, debris count/lifespan, shockwave radius/duration,
    per-layer enabled flags, particle count/lifespan/scale overrides).
  - `resolveJuiceParams(severity): PlayerDeathJuiceParams` — pure, total,
    deterministic; unknown severity falls back to `'respawn'` (never throws).
  - Exported tunable constants in one module: `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_COLOR`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_COUNT`, `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_LIFESPAN_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_DURATION_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers, and `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggles.
- Tests `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` written FIRST (test-first spec).

## Constraints
- Parameter logic is pure: **no Phaser import** in the parameter model.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR` (0x00ffff) per GDD §7.1.
- Intake assumptions: shake duration ~250–400 ms, intensity ~0.008–0.02,
  flash duration ~120–200 ms; keep values inside those bounds.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ intake brief (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Predecessor: AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` constants style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` exists and was written before the implementation; it fails against the pre-change tree.
- [ ] `resolveJuiceParams('respawn')` and `resolveJuiceParams('fatal')` return complete `PlayerDeathJuiceParams` with every field populated.
- [ ] Every asserted `'fatal'` magnitude is strictly greater than the corresponding `'respawn'` magnitude (shake intensity + duration, flash alpha, debris count, shockwave radius).
- [ ] All tunables are exported constants from the single module; no magic numbers remain in the helper.
- [ ] Unknown/invalid severity returns the `'respawn'` parameter set and never throws.
- [ ] `npm test` passes (including the new suite) and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC5 — severity scaling & no behaviour change: the effect is heavier and every tunable is an exported constant.

player-specific cue distinct from the generic enemy `playDestructionSound()` —
plus unit tests. Wiring into scenes is a separate task that depends on the
composed juice helper.

# Screen shake and flash layers

## Goal
Add the two highest-impact juice layers — scene-camera shake and a brief
full-screen flash — as thin Phaser rendering helpers in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`,
tracked in a teardown registry and driven by the parameter model.

## User story
As a player, when my ship is destroyed the camera shakes hard and a bright cyan/
white flash frames the screen, so the moment feels weighty and unmistakable.

## Scope
- `applyShake(scene, params)` — calls `scene.cameras.main.shake(durationMs, intensity)` (full 2D); no-op when the layer toggle is off.
- `spawnDeathFlash(scene, params, registry)` — full-screen overlay (Rectangle/Graphics) at configured alpha/colour that fades to 0 over the configured duration, then destroys itself and splices out of the registry; no-op when disabled.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using `src/test/gameHarness.ts` `bootScene` plus a camera spy.

## Constraints
- No behaviour change to gameplay; cosmetic only.
- Registry contract must mirror the existing `playerExplosions` pattern (`push` on spawn, `splice`/clear on completion and on SHUTDOWN).
- Flash must not block input or swallow pointer events (non-interactive).

## References
- Depends on task "Player-death juice parameter model and constants".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC2, AC4, AC6); GDD §7.1 palette, §7.2 visual style.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Camera spy asserts `shake` is called exactly once with the configured intensity and duration for a `'respawn'` and a `'fatal'` call.
- [ ] The flash is created at the configured alpha/colour, tween duration matches the constant, and it is destroyed and removed from the registry on tween completion.
- [ ] Disabling the shake/flash toggles produces neither a shake call nor a flash object.
- [ ] Existing VFX tests remain green; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

Add two secondary juice layers that outlive the particle burst briefly — debris

# Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point

## Goal
Provide the single shared entry point `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)`
that composes every juice layer (camera shake, dedicated SFX, particle burst,
flash, debris, shockwave) so no scene has to know the layer set, and returns the
handles/registry so teardown can destroy everything.

## User story
As a developer, I call one function with a position and severity and the full
player-death effect plays; each layer is tunable/toggleable in one module and I
cannot accidentally play two sounds or two particle bursts.

## Scope
- `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)` in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`:
  - resolves params via `resolveJuiceParams`;
  - plays `playPlayerDestructionSound()` exactly once;
  - calls `applyShake`, `spawnDeathFlash`, `spawnDeathDebris`, `spawnDeathShockwave`;
  - delegates particles to the existing `spawnExplosionParticles(scene, x, y, SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE, { patterns: resolvePatterns('player'), registry, ...severityOverrides })`;
  - returns a handle `{ params, registry }` (registry is the caller-owned array).
- `options` allows injecting the registry and a seed for deterministic tests.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using the scene harness plus spies on the audio module and `spawnExplosionParticles`.

## Constraints
- The generic `playDestructionSound()` must NOT be called by this helper.
- Exactly one particle burst and exactly one dedicated sound per invocation.
- No gameplay state reads/writes; purely cosmetic.
- Keep the existing `_spawnPlayerExplosion` particle call as the particle source
  (the helper delegates) to avoid duplicate spawns when scenes are migrated.

## References
- Depends on the parameter model, dedicated SFX, shake/flash, and debris/shockwave tasks.
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single call produces shake + exactly one dedicated sound call + particles + flash + debris + shockwave.
- [ ] `playDestructionSound()` is not called by the helper (spy assertion).
- [ ] Particles are spawned via `spawnExplosionParticles` with the `'player'` patterns and the caller's registry.
- [ ] The returned registry contains every juice-owned display object and is suitable for SHUTDOWN teardown.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC1 — shared player-death juice helper exists: a reusable helper composes the full effect and both player-death paths use it.

# Wire PlayScene lose-life path

## Goal
Route the real-run player death (`PlayScene._loseLife`) through
`spawnPlayerDeathJuice`, using severity `'fatal'` for a run-ending death (final
life/game over) and `'respawn'` otherwise, while leaving the wave-timeout
penalty and shield-absorb paths unchanged.

## User story
As a player, losing my final life feels heavier than a mid-run respawn, and a
life lost in the real run has both the shake, the dedicated boom and the
explosion.

## Scope

dedicated sound replaces the generic cue on those paths, and that no scene
leaks juice-owned objects across a stop/restart.

and that no display object survives a scene restart.

# Make the AI config collapsable

## Problem statement

Every gym scene renders a plain-DOM tuning panel (ship config, enemy AI config, boss config) pinned to the bottom-left of the viewport. The enemy AI panel in particular is ~21 rows tall and, even though it is height-capped and scrolls internally, it permanently occupies a large part of the screen and obscures the game view. Designers and testers need to be able to collapse the panel down to a header so they can see the entire screen, then expand it again when they want to tune values.

**Provenance:** migrated from ContextHub work item `WL-0MU1QV98Z004CFBI` (removed there). Original seed text: "In gym scenes the AI config control should be collabsable so that we can see the entire screen."

## Users

- **Game designer / developer** tuning ship/enemy/boss configs in the gym scenes, who needs to toggle the tuning panel out of the way to inspect the full scene, then bring it back without reloading.
- **QA / playtester** verifying gym scenes, who wants the panel collapsed while playing and expanded while editing.

### User stories

- As a designer tuning an enemy in the gym, I want to collapse the AI config panel to a header so I can see the whole scene, and expand it again to continue tuning.
- As a tester, I want a consistent collapse control on every gym panel (Player, Enemies, Boss) so the interaction is predictable.
- As a keyboard-only user, I want to activate the collapse control without a mouse.

## Existing state

- Three gym scenes build a plain-DOM panel that carries the shared `.gym-panel` class (bottom-left anchoring, `max-height: calc(100vh - 120px)`, `overflow-y: auto`, `AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF`):
  - `#gym-config-panel` — `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` (ship config).
  - `#enemy-gym-panel` — `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` (enemy AI config; the tallest).
  - `#boss-gym-panel` — `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` (Central AI boss config).
- There is currently **no** collapse/expand control and no shared panel header/body structure; each scene appends controls directly to the panel element.
- The stylesheet/anchoring contract is regression-tested in `src/style.test.ts`; per-scene tests assert panel DOM ids and `data-config` selectors.
- This is a leaf work item (no children); the AC coverage review returns `proceed`.

## Desired change

Add a single shared, reusable collapse/expand affordance to all three gym panels:

- A shared helper wraps each panel's existing children in a `.gym-panel-body` element and prepends a `.gym-panel-header` containing a native `<button class="gym-panel-toggle">` (with a short title/label and `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`).
- Clicking the toggle flips a `data-collapsed` attribute on the panel; CSS hides `.gym-panel-body` when `data-collapsed="true"`, leaving only the header visible in the bottom-left.
- Panels start **expanded** in every scene; no cross-scene/reload persistence (deliberately deferred).
- All existing DOM ids, `data-config` / `data-config-value` selectors and control DOM order are preserved so current tests and behaviour are unaffected when expanded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Collapse control present on every gym panel, default expanded.** Each of `#gym-config-panel`, `#enemy-gym-panel` and `#boss-gym-panel` renders a header containing a native `<button class="gym-panel-toggle">` with `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` pointing at its `.gym-panel-body`; the panel starts with `data-collapsed="false"` and its controls are visible.
- [ ] **AC2 — Toggle collapses and expands.** Activating the toggle sets `data-collapsed="true"`, sets `aria-expanded="false"` and hides the body; activating it again restores the expanded state. Verified by simulated `click` DOM tests in happy-dom.
- [ ] **AC3 — CSS contract for the collapsed state.** `src/style.css` hides `.gym-panel[data-collapsed="true"] .gym-panel-body` while keeping the `.gym-panel-header` visible, so a collapsed panel shrinks to its header only; regression-tested (computed style) in `src/style.test.ts`. The bottom-left anchoring / `max-height` contract from AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC4 — No regression to existing panel DOM.** Wrapping children in `.gym-panel-body` preserves every existing element id, `data-config` / `data-config-value` selector and control DOM order, and the existing per-scene panel tests continue to pass unchanged where they assert behaviour (selectors updated only where they assumed direct children).
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests, typecheck and build.** New unit tests cover the shared helper (wrap children, toggle state, accessibility attributes), per-scene tests cover the toggle on all three panels, `npm test` passes, and `npm run build` (tsc + vite) succeeds.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated.** `README.md` (gym-panel notes) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.5 document the shared collapse control, its classes/attribute and default-expanded behaviour.

## Constraints

- **No persistence:** the collapsed/expanded state resets to expanded on each scene start (decision Q3 = a). localStorage persistence and a keyboard shortcut are out of scope and should be captured as follow-ups if wanted.
- **Plain DOM only:** the control must work in the existing happy-dom test environment (native `<button>`, no Phaser UI), matching the current panel implementation.
- **Preserve the shared `.gym-panel` contract:** anchoring, `max-height` and internal scrolling from AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF must not change.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/gymPanel.ts` — **new**: shared `makeCollapsible({ panel, title })` helper plus exported class constants (`gym-panel-header`, `gym-panel-body`, `gym-panel-toggle`) and the `data-collapsed` attribute name; moves existing children into the body and prepends the header/toggle.
- `src/utils/gymPanel.test.ts` — **new**: unit tests for the helper.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — `_buildPanel()` calls the helper (title e.g. "Ship Config").
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — `_buildPanel()` calls the helper (title e.g. "AI Config").
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — `_buildPanel()` calls the helper (title e.g. "Boss Config").
- `src/style.css` — header/toggle styling and `.gym-panel[data-collapsed="true"] .gym-panel-body { display: none; }`.
- `src/style.test.ts` — regression test for the collapsed CSS contract.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — toggle presence/behaviour per scene.
- `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.5 — docs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Test-breakage risk:** tests that assume panel controls are direct children could break when children are wrapped in `.gym-panel-body`. Mitigation: descendant `querySelector` calls (the dominant pattern) are unaffected; update any direct-child selector to target the body.
- **Discovery risk:** a fully collapsed header must still make the toggle obviously clickable. Mitigation: keep the header visible with a clear label and toggle affordance.
- **Scope-creep risk:** persistence, keyboard shortcuts, animation and "remember last state" are attractive but explicitly out of scope; record them as separate follow-up work items rather than expanding this change.
- **Assumption:** the feature applies to all three gym panels via one shared helper (decision Q1 = a), and the collapsed form is a header bar (decision Q2 = a).

## Related work

- `Enemy design UI covers Gym scene buttons` (AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF) — established the shared `.gym-panel` bottom-left anchoring / `max-height` contract this change extends.
- `Gym editor panel with live tuning (Save / Save As)` (AH-0MTHG5BIB006PP0P) — built the `GymEnemies` editor panel.
- `Gym scene sliders bound to live ship config` (AH-0MTA8DMBH007MEHG) and `Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship` (AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V) — built the `GymPlayer` panel.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope: which panels gain the collapse control?** Options: (a) all `.gym-panel` panels; (b) only `#enemy-gym-panel`; (c) only the AI panels (`#enemy-gym-panel` + `#boss-gym-panel`). **Recommended: (a).**
  - **Answer (operator): "1. a"** — all `.gym-panel` panels. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: the shared class makes it one implementation and matches "gym scenes" (plural).
- **Q2 — What does "collapsed" look like?** Options: (a) header bar + toggle button hiding the body; (b) fully hidden panel with a floating "Show config" button; (c) icon-only chip. **Recommended: (a).**
  - **Answer (operator): "2/ a"** — header bar + toggle button. Source: interactive reply. Keeps the panel discoverable and testable via a stable selector while freeing the screen.
- **Q3 — Toggle behaviour and state?** Options: (a) toggle button only, starts expanded, no persistence; (b) toggle + persist collapsed state; (c) toggle + keyboard shortcut + persistence. **Recommended: (a).**
  - **Answer (operator): "3. a"** — toggle button only, default expanded, no persistence. Source: interactive reply. Minimal change satisfying "see the entire screen"; persistence/shortcut deferred.
- **Open items:** none. Intake was initially paused for producer review (comment `AH-C0MUGZF7LN009WJP4`) and resumed once the operator supplied the three answers above.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUDIV437000U4NY** – Design and implement the pure difficulty scorer module (src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts) (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNKXX001XBLJ** – Implement: Docs — player-in-enemy-gym convention (completed)
- **AH-0MTCPL9NA0025ZUI** – In-Game spawning should not be round robin (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: able, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+255 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: able, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+233 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muayb7o4009lwbf, 100vh, 120px, able, ac1 (+228 more)

# Intake Brief — Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123)

- **Type:** feature
- **Priority:** medium
- **Status:** in-progress (intake)
- **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Asteroids are currently placed only as a single fixed formation group in
Level 1 Wave 1. The design calls for asteroids to be a persistent,
escalating roaming hazard: in **every** regular wave of every level, asteroids
should spawn at **random offscreen positions** and drift into the playfield,
with their **frequency growing slowly** as levels and waves progress. This
increases surviving pressure and variety without adding a new enemy archetype.

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, I want asteroids to appear unpredictably from offscreen
  during every wave so that the playfield always carries a drifting hazard.
- **As a player**, I want the asteroid threat to grow slowly as I progress
  through levels and waves, so difficulty rises without sudden spikes.
- **As a player**, I want variety in asteroid size (more medium rocks early,
  more large rocks later), so the split-chain risk develops over a run.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` implements the E6 Asteroid: constant-velocity
  straight-line drift, four-edge wrap, continuous rotation, three size tiers
  (`large` / `medium` / `small`), split-on-destroy (large→2 medium→2 small),
  never fires. The constructor accepts optional `vx`/`vy` and `sizeTier`.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` places exactly one asteroid via
  `group('asteroid', 'single', 1, { startX: GAME_WIDTH * 0.6, startY: GAME_HEIGHT * 0.25 })`
  in Level 1 Wave 1 only. Every other wave has no asteroids.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` spawns wave groups from
  `WaveManager.planSpawns()`; asteroids roam via
  `Asteroid.updatePosition(dt)`, are shootable during transitions, survive
  wave timeouts, are cleared on boss entry, and are registered with
  `WaveManager.registerDynamicSpawn()` so wave-clear accounting includes them.
  `PlayScene` already exposes an injectable `rng` (`setRng`) and drives the
  simulation through the deterministic public `tick(dt)`.
- `WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS = 30` (`PlayScene.ts`); each wave runs a 30 s
  countdown (`waveTimer`).
- No existing spawn-scheduler module; there is no test for random asteroid
  spawn timings or weight progression.

## Desired change

Add a **random offscreen asteroid spawner** that operates during every
regular wave. It is a pure planner (new `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts`) plus a
small `PlayScene` integration that releases planned spawns as the wave timer
elapses.

### Spawn plan (pure, RNG-injected)

For a given cumulative **global wave index** `g` (0-based across the whole
campaign, incremented once per regular wave):

1. **Per-wave count** starts at `2` and **doubles** each time the large weight
   threshold is reached: `2 → 4 → 8 → …`.
2. **Size weighting** per wave:
   - medium weight is fixed at `80`;
   - large weight starts at `20` and increases by `+20` per wave;
   - when large weight reaches `2 × medium` (i.e. `160`), the weights **reset**
     to `medium 80 / large 20` and the per-wave count doubles.
   - Size tier is drawn per asteroid from these weights (baseline 80:20
     medium:large).
3. **Spawn timing** (fraction of `WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS`):
   - `N` asteroids divide the wave into `N` equal segments;
   - anchor for asteroid `i` is `i / N`; a small random jitter (≈ ±5 %) is
     applied and clamped to `[0, 0.95]`;
   - the **first** asteroid is additionally constrained to the first `10 %`
     of the wave;
   - with the baseline `N = 2` this puts the first within 0–10 % and the
     second around 50 %.

### Offscreen origin and drift

- Choose a **random edge** uniformly from top / bottom / left / right.
- Place the asteroid at a random point along that edge, offset **outward**
  (offscreen) by `asteroid half-size + margin` so it is fully outside the
  viewport at spawn.
- Give it an **inward-directed** velocity (perpendicular to the edge, with up
  to ≈ ±30° spread) at the tier's canonical speed, guaranteeing the inward
  component dominates so it enters the playfield promptly.
- `Asteroid.vx`/`vy` continue to drive straight-line motion + four-edge wrap.

### Escalation semantics

- The global wave index is monotonic across the campaign; the large weight
  rises **once per wave**. Under the shipped 5-level campaign
  (2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 13 waves) the count is `2` for waves 0–6 and `4` for
  waves 7–12, with the weight cycle resetting at the count change.
- Boss encounter: **no** random asteroid spawns (existing boss-entry cleanup
  continues to destroy carried-over asteroids).

### Replacement of the fixed group

- Remove the fixed `group('asteroid', 'single', 1, …)` from Level 1 Wave 1 in
  `Formations.ts`; all asteroids now come from the random spawner. Update the
  existing `WaveManager.test.ts` assertion that Level 1 Wave 1 contains an
  asteroid group.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every regular wave of every level (Levels 1–5) spawns asteroids from the random offscreen spawner; the boss encounter spawns none.
- A wave begins with 2 asteroids by default; every spawned asteroid appears **offscreen** (fully outside the viewport on a random edge) and drifts inward into the playfield.
- Spawn timing: the first asteroid spawns within the first 10 % of the wave window and the second around 50 %; for higher counts spawn times are spread across the wave with randomised jitter and remain ordered/non-duplicated.
- Size weighting: asteroids are large or medium, weighted toward medium (baseline 80:20). The large weight increases by +20 each wave; when it reaches 2× the medium weight, weights reset to 80:20 and the per-wave count doubles (2 → 4 → 8 → …).
- Spawned asteroids are registered with `WaveManager` as dynamic spawns so wave-clear accounting includes them, and existing asteroid behaviours (splitting, timeout survival, transition collidability, boss-entry cleanup) are preserved.
- The fixed asteroid group is removed from Level 1 Wave 1; all asteroids now originate from the spawner.
- Unit tests cover the pure planner deterministically (injected RNG): count progression, weight escalation/reset, timing segments, offscreen edge/position selection, and inward velocity. Integration tests in `PlayScene.test.ts` cover spawn timing against `tick(dt)`, offscreen positions, and boss exclusion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.1 / §4.2) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§1.2).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Pure logic must remain free of Phaser runtime dependencies so it is
  unit-testable (mirror the `WaveManager` / `Formations` pattern).
- All randomness must flow through the scene's injectable `rng` to keep tests
  deterministic; the planner takes an `rng` parameter.
- Must not spawn while paused or during a wave/level transition, and must not
  break existing asteroid timeout/carry-over or boss-entry cleanup behaviour.
- Keep the spawner tuning in exported constants so it is easy to retune.
- Build → test → commit order only; no `main` branch changes (dev only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — **new** pure planner: weight escalation +
  count doubling, timing segments, offscreen edge/position + inward velocity.
- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.test.ts` — **new** deterministic unit tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — integrate the planner into `tick(dt)`; track
  elapsed wave time and release due spawns; extend `spawnAsteroidAt` (or add a
  helper) to accept velocity; skip paused/transition/boss phases.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — integration tests (timing, offscreen,
  boss exclusion, dynamic registration).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — remove the fixed Level 1 Wave 1 asteroid group.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — add a pure `globalWaveIndex` accessor (or
  equivalent) so the planner can key escalation to campaign progress.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — update the Level 1 Wave 1 asteroid
  assertion.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — verify velocity injection path (no behaviour
  change expected).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` —
  document the new spawn mechanic.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** escalation is keyed to the cumulative global wave index
  across the campaign (not per-level resets), and the 13-wave shipped campaign
  reaches count 4 within a normal run.
- **Assumption:** "random edge" = uniform over the four screen edges; offscreen
  margin is a tunable constant (`half-size + small margin`).
- **Risk — wave stalls / asteroid accumulation:** more asteroids (plus large
  split chains = up to 7 kills each) can slow wave clearing, and asteroids
  survive timeouts and carry over, so their number can grow across waves.
  *Mitigation:* keep speeds slow, document tuning constants, and flag a
  possible concurrency cap / carry-over limit as a follow-up work item if
  playtesting shows a stall.
- **Risk — shallow inward velocity** could let an asteroid wrap before
  entering; *mitigation:* bias the velocity perpendicular to the spawn edge
  and clamp the angular spread.
- **Risk — non-determinism in tests:** *mitigation:* inject `rng` everywhere.

# Hold-full Power-up Choice Dialog — Opaque Backdrop

## Problem Statement

The `MineralChoiceScene` overlay (shown when the ship's mineral hold fills and the player must choose a power-up) currently uses a translucent black backdrop (`alpha: 0.75`), allowing the paused game field to remain visible behind the dialog. The requirement is for the backdrop to be fully opaque, blanking out the entire screen behind the choice dialog.

## Users

- **Player** — When the hold fills, the choice dialog should be clearly visually separated from the gameplay field by a fully black screen, improving focus on the choice options.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Opaque backdrop** — The `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` constant in `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` is set to `1.0` (fully opaque), replacing the current value of `0.75`.
2. **Visual result** — When `MineralChoiceScene` is displayed, the entire screen behind the choice options is solid black (no transparency).
3. **No visual regressions** — The power-up choice text and option labels remain clearly readable and unchanged in appearance.
4. **All tests pass** — The full project test suite passes, including `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`.

## Constraints

- This is a minimal, surgical change: only the backdrop alpha value is modified.
- No API changes, no new parameters, no behavioural changes to choice selection logic.
- The fix applies to both the main game (`PlayScene` → `MineralChoiceScene`) and the gym scenes where the choice overlay may be launched.

## Existing State

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` defines `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA = 0.75` on line ~40.
- The backdrop is drawn as a full-screen black rectangle: `this.add.rectangle(0, 0, GAME_WIDTH, GAME_HEIGHT, 0x000000, CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA)`.
- The comment above the constant describes it as "Translucent backdrop so the paused field remains visible behind."

## Desired Change

- Set `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` to `1.0`.
- Update the comment to reflect the opaque/blanked-out behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — Change `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` from `0.75` to `1.0` and update its comment.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — Verify existing tests pass (no test changes expected; the backdrop alpha is not directly tested).

## Related Work

- **AH-0MUCST52T003AX4V** — "Choice modal scene and PlayScene mineral wiring" (parent feature that created this scene).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — "Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold and grant a power-up choice" (epic that introduced the hold-full mechanic).
- **AH-0MUCST2VY004T6QQ** — "Test: Hold-full choice scene and PlayScene wiring" (tests for the choice scene).
- **AH-0MUCST5W9009BH34** — "Documentation and full project test suite validation" (test validation).

# Change the current mineral count to a bar that fills

## Problem statement

The ship's hold (minerals collected) is currently shown on the HUD as a text counter (`Minerals: n/20`). A text counter is visually weak in the neon-vector aesthetic and does not communicate "filling up" at a glance. Replace it with a fixed-length, hollow-outlined bar that fills proportionally as minerals are collected.

## Users

**Player** — needs to read hold progress instantly during fast play, without parsing digits.

- As a player, I want the hold shown as a bar that fills as I collect minerals, so that I can gauge progress toward the next power-up choice at a glance.
- As a player, I want the bar to show an empty hollow outline when I have no minerals, so that I can tell the hold exists and is empty.
- As a player, I want the bar to be the same length at all times, so that the layout does not shift and the relationship between fill and capacity stays readable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Bar replaces text.** When a mineral capacity is configured, the HUD renders a fixed-length horizontal bar row (outline + fill) in place of the `Minerals: n/20` text. The `Minerals:` text label is no longer the primary representation.
2. **Hollow when empty.** At `minerals = 0` only the hollow outline is visible (no fill pixels). The outline uses the existing neon HUD palette (cyan `#00ffff`).
3. **Proportional fill.** The filled portion grows linearly from the left: `0` at empty, full inner width at `minerals === capacity`; the fill width is clamped so it never exceeds or bleeds outside the outline. Any non-zero value renders a visible minimum fill so single-digit progress is perceptible.
4. **Stable row layout.** The bar row is hidden entirely when `capacity === 0` (gyms/game states without the mineral mechanic). The lives row and active effect/weapon rows keep their current positions with no overlap.
5. **Existing hold mechanics unchanged.** `GameState` arithmetic (`addMinerals`, `isHoldFull`, `resolveHold`, overflow) and the hold-full power-up choice are unaffected; the HUD only changes how the same values are rendered.
6. **Validated by unit tests.** A unit test asserts bar geometry at empty (`0/20`), mid (`10/20`) and full (`20/20`), the hollow-at-empty outline state, clamping at/over capacity, and row visibility for `capacity = 0`.
7. **Validation in-scene.** The `GymMinerals` gym and `PlayScene` show the bar filling as minerals are collected (manual/visual verification; `GymMinerals` test updated to assert the bar state instead of the removed text).
8. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the Game Design Document §4.4.1 hold description (replace `Minerals: n/20` references with the bar). CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must stay framework-idiomatic: the HUD is a `Phaser.GameObjects.Container`; the bar should be drawn with `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` (consistent with existing icon drawing), not DOM/CSS.
- Must not break the standalone-HUD contract: `src/ui/HUD.ts` has no gym-specific imports and binds to any scene.
- Must respect the neon aesthetic: "dark background with glowing neon outlines, minimal fill" (GDD §Visual Aesthetic).
- No new runtime dependency.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` owns the mineral row via `_mineralLabel` (a `Text` object), `setMineralStore(minerals, capacity)`, `getMineralLabel()`, and `getMineralStoreValue()`. The row is shown when `_mineralCapacity > 0` and positioned below the lives row in `refresh()`.
- `src/core/GameState.ts` owns the authoritative hold (`minerals`, `mineralCapacity`, `addMinerals`, `isHoldFull`, `resolveHold`).
- Callers: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_syncMineralHud`), `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`.
- Tests referencing the text contract: `src/ui/__tests__/HUD.minerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts` (`getMineralLabel()` matching `/^Minerals: \d+\/20$/`).
- Docs referencing the text: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.1.

## Desired change

`HUD` draws a fixed-size bar (predicted: ~120 px outline width × ~10 px height, exposed as named constants so it is tunable) at the existing mineral-row Y offset:

- Outer outline always drawn when `capacity > 0`, hollow at `minerals = 0`.
- Inner fill width = `round(innerWidth * clamp(minerals / capacity, 0, 1))`, with a small minimum fill for `minerals > 0`.
- Bar row hidden when `capacity = 0`.
- Public test accessor (e.g. `getMineralBarState(): { filled: number; total: number; visible: boolean }`) added; `getMineralStoreValue()` retained. `getMineralLabel()` is removed or repurposed as part of this change and its callers/tests updated.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Replace `_mineralLabel` text row with a `Graphics`-drawn outline + fill bar; add bar geometry constants and `getMineralBarState()`; update row visibility/positioning.
- `src/ui/__tests__/HUD.minerals.test.ts` — Update to assert bar geometry (empty/mid/full), hollow outline, clamping, and hidden-when-capacity-0.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts` — Replace the `getMineralLabel()` text assertion with a bar-state assertion.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Confirm `_syncMineralHud` continues to drive the bar (likely no change beyond accessor usage).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Confirm `setMineralStore` call-sites need no change.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §4.4.1 hold description (`Minerals: n/20` → filling bar).
- `README.md` — Update the HUD counter reference.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the bar *replaces* the numeric counter as the primary representation (per "change the current mineral count to a bar"); no numeric overlay is added. The underlying value remains exposed via `getMineralStoreValue()` and the new bar-state accessor.
- **Assumption:** bar dimensions/colours are implementation details to be tuned to the existing HUD row height (`HUD_ROW_HEIGHT = 22`).
- **Assumption:** the same HUD bar serves `PlayScene` and the gyms (the HUD already shares this row).
- **Risk (low):** HUD row-offset regression could overlap lives/effect rows — mitigated by AC4 tests and existing HUD tests.
- **Risk (low):** gym/PlayScene tests asserting the old text will fail until updated — captured in AC6/AC7 and the Key Files list.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adding numeric overlay, animation/easing of the fill, or colour changes at capacity are out of scope; record as separate work items if wanted.

## Related work

- Parent/related context: `Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold and grant a power-up choice` (AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q) and its completed children (`AH-0MUCST45Q0054X19` HUD counter, `AH-0MUCST23S006AAMC` HUD counter tests).
- This change supersedes the text-counter rendering introduced by `AH-0MUCST45Q0054X19` (the hold store/overflow/HUD counter) while leaving its arithmetic intact.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U** – Redesign P7 Dash: make collectable teleport power-up (completed)
- **AH-0MTV7OAJM002GGMM** – Move control buttons for gym scenes to the bottom (completed)
- **AH-0MUCST52T003AX4V** – Choice modal scene and PlayScene mineral wiring (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: bar, change, collected, count, current (+10 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: bar, change, collected, consistent, count (+10 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: bar, change, count, current, currently (+9 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Should the numeric count remain (e.g. alongside or inside the bar), or should the bar fully replace the text? — **Answer (producer):** full replacement — the bar replaces the numeric text as the primary representation; the underlying value remains accessible programmatically via `getMineralStoreValue()` and the new `getMineralBarState()`. Source: producer reply to intake review (confirming the documented assumption).
- **Q:** What length/height/colour should the bar be? — **Answer (producer):** implementation detail — tune to the existing HUD row (predicted ~120 px × ~10 px, cyan neon outline), exposed as named constants. Source: producer reply to intake review (confirming the documented assumption).

# Add bullet TTL to enemy configurator

## Problem statement

The Enemy Gym configurator exposes a slider for every shot-behaviour field
except bullet time-to-live (TTL), even though `EnemyConfig.bulletLifetime` is
already a persisted CSV column and is plumbed through the entity firing seam.
As a result a designer cannot tune TTL from the gym, and the difficulty scorer
ignores TTL entirely — an archetype that sprays long-lived bullets (which wrap
the screen and stay lethal) is scored identically to one whose bullets expire
almost immediately. This work item closes both gaps: a TTL slider in the enemy
configurator, and TTL as a positive contributor to the enemy difficulty index
(higher TTL ⇒ higher difficulty).

## Users

- **Level designer / content author** — tunes enemy bullet lifetime from the
  Enemy Gym and immediately sees the effect on the live difficulty readout.
- **Reviewer / producer** — needs the difficulty model to account for bullet
  persistence so the campaign ordering stays auditable as archetypes are
  retuned.

Example user stories:

- *As a level designer, I want a TTL slider in the Enemy Gym enemy panel, so
  that I can tune how long enemy bullets persist without editing the CSV by
  hand.*
- *As a level designer, I want the difficulty score to rise when I increase
  TTL, so that a long-lived-bullet archetype is measured as harder than the
  same archetype with short-lived bullets.*
- *As a reviewer, I want the campaign difficulty ordering to remain
  non-decreasing after TTL is added as a factor, so that the intended
  progression cannot silently invert.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — TTL slider in the enemy configurator.** The `GymEnemies` editor panel
  renders a `bulletLifetime` range slider, queryable as
  `input[data-config="bulletLifetime"]`, with a documented min/max/step
  (proposed 0.1–5.0 s, step 0.1 — see Assumptions). It is seeded from the
  active config, updates its value readout and the in-memory `currentConfig`
  on input, and persists through both **Save** and **Save As…** (round-trips
  via the CSV store).
- **AC2 — TTL live-applies to spawned enemies.** Changing the slider
  live-applies the new TTL to already-spawned entities through the existing
  `_bulletLifetime` seam (no respawn required), consistent with the other
  shot-behaviour sliders.
- **AC3 — TTL is a difficulty factor (higher TTL ⇒ higher difficulty).**
  `enemyDifficulty` adds a `bulletLifetime` entry to `FACTOR_WEIGHTS` and
  `FACTOR_RANGES`, normalised so a longer lifetime scores higher. The factor
  appears in both `breakdown` and `factors`, and contributes **zero** when
  firing is suppressed (`shotPattern === 'none'`, or `suppressFiring: true` /
  waves with `shootEnabled: false`), matching the other firing factors.
- **AC4 — Validation tests.** Unit tests assert that increasing `bulletLifetime`
  never decreases the enemy score, that the factor is suppressed for
  non-firing archetypes, and that `breakdown`/`factors` include the new key.
  Scene-level tests cover the slider (present, range, seed, live-apply,
  difficulty-readout change, Save/Save As round-trip). The campaign calibration
  test (`src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`) must still pass — the
  built-in campaign ordering stays non-decreasing.
- **AC5 — Documentation updated.** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §9.2 factor table gains the `bulletLifetime` row (weight, range, inverted?
  no — longer is harder) and §9.4's per-archetype/campaign score tables are
  recomputed. Code comments on the new factor explain the direction and
  suppression rule. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No CSV/format change.** `bulletLifetime` is already a persisted column
  (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) with codec support — do not add a new field or
  break round-trip compatibility.
- **Absolute, deterministic, 0–100.** The difficulty model stays independent of
  player state; weights and ranges remain named constants in one place, and
  tests pin **ordering/monotonicity**, not magic numbers.
- **Weight choice changes the published campaign scores.** Adding a factor
  changes `WEIGHT_SUM`, so the documented §9.4 tables must be recomputed and
  the campaign ordering re-verified.
- **UK English** in all docs and comments.
- Scope discipline: extra opportunities (e.g. making the Boss archetype honour
  `bulletLifetime` instead of the fixed `BOSS_BULLET_LIFETIME`, or adding a
  player-bullet TTL control) are recorded as linked follow-ups, not folded in.

## Existing state

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `EnemyConfig.bulletLifetime: number` already
  exists (documented "Bullet lifetime in seconds").
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed lifetimes: scout/diver/swarm/asteroid
  1.5 s, tank/boss 2.0 s, phaser 1.75 s.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — `bulletLifetime` column present with the above
  values; `src/core/csv.ts` already parses/coerces it.
- `src/entities/*` — Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm all accept
  `bulletLifetime` via `BaseEnemy` (default 1.5 s) and stamp it onto fired
  bullets. **Boss ignores the config value** and uses the module constant
  `BOSS_BULLET_LIFETIME = 2.0`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — `ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES` lists every numeric
  shot/formation field **except** `bulletLifetime`; `_applyLive` does **not**
  patch `_bulletLifetime` (only `_bulletSpeed`, `_fireInterval`,
  `_burstCount`, `_shotProbability`, etc.).
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`/`FACTOR_RANGES` cover nine
  factors (`count`, `driftSpeed`, `shotPattern`, `fireInterval`,
  `shotProbability`, `bulletSpeed`, `burstCount`, `formationKind`,
  `asteroidSplit`); firing factors are zeroed when suppressed.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §9 documents factors, ranges and
  the recomputed campaign table.

## Desired change

1. Add `bulletLifetime` to `ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES` in `GymEnemies.ts`
   (0.1–5.0 s, step 0.1 proposed), placed after `bulletSpeed`. It flows through
   the existing generic slider row / read / apply / persist code paths with no
   special-casing.
2. Add `bulletLifetime` handling to `_applyLive` so spawned entities pick up
   the new value live (mirrors `_bulletSpeed`).
3. Add a `bulletLifetime` factor to `enemyDifficulty.ts`:
   - `FACTOR_WEIGHTS.bulletLifetime` (proposed 6 — comparable to the
     `bulletSpeed` weight; a documented, tunable opinion),
   - `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletLifetime = { min: 0.1, max: 5.0 }` (matching the
     slider so designers stay inside the normalised range),
   - normalised directly (higher value ⇒ higher factor), suppressed with the
     other firing factors.
4. Add/extend tests as per AC4.
5. Recompute and update the §9 documentation tables.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Add `bulletLifetime` to `ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES`; add `_bulletLifetime` to the `_applyLive` patch list.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — Add `bulletLifetime` to `FACTOR_WEIGHTS` and `FACTOR_RANGES`; compute it in the firing-factor branch; verify suppression.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — Slider presence/range/seed/live-apply/difficulty-readout/Save/Save-As tests.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.test.ts` — Monotonicity, suppression and breakdown-coverage tests for the new factor.
- `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts` — Confirm the non-decreasing campaign ordering still holds (likely no code change).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §9.2 factor table row and recomputed §9.4 tables.

## Related work

- **Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K)** — the difficulty-scoring design this item extends; its AC2 factor list did not include TTL.
- **Design and implement the pure difficulty scorer module (AH-0MUDIV437000U4NY)** — implementation of `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`.
- **Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0)** — introduced `bulletLifetime` plumbing and wrap/expiry semantics; reduced TTL by 50%.
- **shotProbability slider in the enemy gym (AH-0MU0F1T2H003B4K0)** — direct precedent for adding a shot-behaviour slider plus its tests.
- **Make the AI config collapsible (AH-0MUDYFMUX007Q0W3)** — the collapsible enemy panel the slider lives in.
- **Enemy gym scene / editor panel (AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4 / AH-0MTHG5BIB006PP0P)** — the `GymEnemies` scene and panel.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (range):** TTL slider range 0.1–5.0 s, step 0.1. Rationale: seed
  lifetimes cluster at 1.5–2.0 s; the range comfortably brackets them while
  keeping the difficulty normalisation meaningful. **Producer may adjust.**
- **Assumption (weight):** `bulletLifetime` weight 6 (same order as
  `bulletSpeed = 5`). TTL is a moderate, secondary hazard axis that compounds
  with speed and burst. **Producer may adjust**; tests must pin monotonicity,
  not the number.
- **Assumption (semantics):** "TTL" means the existing `bulletLifetime`
  (seconds) — no new field is introduced.
- **Risk (score drift):** every published archetype/campaign score changes
  because `WEIGHT_SUM` grows. Mitigation: recompute the §9.4 tables and keep
