# Gym scenes index not navigable by keyboard (AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE)

## Problem statement

The dev-mode **Gym Index** (`GymIndex`) renders every gym scene, enemy
config, boss row and dev-utility tool as clickable text rows, but the rows
only respond to **pointer** events (`pointerdown`). A player or developer who
navigates by keyboard alone cannot move focus between rows or launch any gym
scene from the index — there is no default focus, no visible focus highlight,
and no Enter/Space activation. This breaks the keyboard-only control
guarantee already delivered for the rest of the game (Menu, GameOver, Pause,
Help, Leaderboard).

## Users

Developers/testers who exercise the gym scenes and keyboard-only/accessibility
users who expect the in-canvas UI to be fully operable without a mouse.

**User stories**

- As a keyboard-only developer, I want the Gym Index rows to be reachable with
  Tab / arrow keys and show a clear focus highlight, so that I always know
  which gym scene Enter will launch.
- As a keyboard-only user, I want Enter/Space on a focused row to launch the
  same scene a mouse click would, so that I never need a pointing device to
  use the gym.
- As a keyboard-only user, I want ESC to still return to the main menu and
  mouse clicks to keep working, so that existing navigation is not regressed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Every row is focusable with a visible default focus.** On
  `GymIndex.create()`, every rendered row across all four columns (plain
  scenes, ENEMIES, Bosses, Dev Utilities) is registered with the shared
  `FocusManager`; exactly one row is focused by default and visibly
  highlighted (bright colour + stroke), all others rendered unfocused.
  *Verification:* unit test asserts the focused index/count and the
  `setStyle` focus highlight on the default row.
- **AC2 — Focus cycles with wrap-around.** `Tab` and `ArrowDown`/`ArrowRight`
  move focus forward; `Shift+Tab` and `ArrowUp`/`ArrowLeft` move focus
  backward, through the rows in reading order (left→right columns, top→bottom
  within a column), wrapping at both ends. *Verification:* unit test emits
  `keydown` events and asserts the focused row changes in the expected order
  and wraps.
- **AC3 — Enter/Space activates the focused row identically to a click.**
  Activation starts the correct scene for each row flavour: plain scene rows
  start their scene key; enemy-config rows start `GymEnemies` with
  `{ enemyKey }`; the dedicated `GymBoss` ("Boss") and Dev Utility rows start
  their `sceneKey` directly. Focus does not move on activation.
  *Verification:* unit test activates each row flavour and asserts the target
  scene/key/params.
- **AC4 — No pointer or ESC regression; no listener leak.** Existing
  `pointerdown` navigation for every row still works, ESC still returns to the
  main menu (`addBackToMenuOnEsc`), and scene `SHUTDOWN` detaches the focus
  keyboard listener and clears the registry (safe re-entry on restart).
  *Verification:* unit test reuses the existing pointer tests, asserts ESC
  navigation, and asserts `FocusManager.shutdown()` ran on shutdown.
- **AC5 — Keyboard tests added/updated.** `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` gains
  tests covering default focus, forward/backward cycling including wrap,
  activation per row flavour, and shutdown cleanup. The existing *“non-ESC key
  does not switch scenes”* test is updated to use an inert non-activation key
  (not `Enter`), and all existing GymIndex tests remain green.
- **AC6 — Docs and on-screen hint updated.** The `GymIndex` module doc comment
  and the on-screen `GYM_INDEX_HINT` are updated to mention the keyboard
  controls (Tab/arrows to move, Enter/Space to select); any README or
  ESC-navigation documentation that enumerates keyboard-navigable screens is
  updated to include the Gym Index.
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The Gym Index is a **dev-mode** scene; no gameplay behaviour changes.
- Reuse the existing shared `FocusManager` (`src/utils/focusManager.ts`) —
  do **not** add ad-hoc per-scene key handling. It already drives MenuScene,
  GameOverScene, PauseScene, HelpScene and LeaderboardScene.
- Layout, discovery (`import.meta.glob`) and column ordering must not change.
- Keyboard support is **additive**: pointer handlers and ESC behaviour stay
  intact.
- No CI/CD pipeline tests (per intake convention).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` builds four columns of `Phaser.GameObjects.Text`
  rows and wires each with `setInteractive({ useHandCursor: true })` +
  `on('pointerdown', …)`. There is no `FocusManager`, no default focus and no
  key handling other than `addBackToMenuOnEsc(this)`.
- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` provides `register`, `attachKeyboard`,
  `cycleFocus`, `activateFocused`, `getFocusedIndex`, `shutdown`. It maps
  `Tab`/`ArrowDown`/`ArrowRight` → forward and `Shift+Tab`/`ArrowUp`/
  `ArrowLeft` → backward (linear, wrap-around), and `Enter`/`Space` →
  activation.
- The keyboard-only convention is already established and tested in
  `MenuScene`, `GameOverScene`, `PauseScene`, `HelpScene` and
  `LeaderboardScene` (parent AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9).
- An existing test, *“pressing a non-ESC key does not switch scenes”*, uses
  `Enter` as its “non-ESC” key. After this change `Enter` activates the
  focused row, so this test must be updated to use a genuinely inert key
  (e.g. `q`).

## Desired change

In `GymIndex.create()`:

1. Instantiate a `FocusManager`.
2. Register each row (in every column, reading order) with its activation
   callback, reusing the same logic as the existing `pointerdown` handler
   (extract a small `activate(entry)` helper so pointer and keyboard share one
   code path).
3. Call `focusManager.attachKeyboard(this)` and detach via
   `this.events.once(Phaser.Scenes.Events.SHUTDOWN, () => this.focusManager.shutdown())`.
4. Keep `addBackToMenuOnEsc(this)` as-is.
5. Update `GYM_INDEX_HINT` to advertise the keyboard controls.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — register index rows with `FocusManager`, share
  the activation path between pointer and keyboard, update hint text/doc.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — add keyboard-navigation tests (default
  focus, cycling + wrap, activation per row flavour, shutdown cleanup).
- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` — reused as-is (no change expected).
- `README.md` / ESC-navigation docs — add Gym Index to the keyboard-navigable
  screens if enumerated.

## Risks

- **Existing ESC test regresses.** The current “non-ESC key” test uses
  `Enter`; it will start a scene once activation lands. Mitigation: update
  that test to an inert key (AC5).
- **Scope creep.** 2-D/grid navigation, additional keyboard shortcuts, or
  mouse-free `GymEnemies`/gym-scene internals are out of scope here — record
  them as linked follow-up work items rather than expanding this change.
- **Shared-utility coupling.** `FocusManager` is used by five other scenes;
  this change must consume it without modifying its public behaviour.

## Assumptions

- **Linear, not grid, navigation.** Rows cycle linearly in reading order
  (matching every other scene's `FocusManager` usage) rather than using
  2-D column/row arrow navigation. A grid model would require extending the
  shared `FocusManager`; that is out of scope and can be raised as a follow-up
  if the linear model proves awkward. *This is reversible: no API/layout
  changes are needed to switch later.*
- Focus cycling order is left→right by column, top→bottom within a column
  (plain scenes → ENEMIES → Bosses → Dev Utilities).
- Focus styling uses the `FocusManager` defaults; row background colours stay
  unchanged.
- No new scene or discovery behaviour is required.

## Related work

- AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9 — Keyboard only control (parent umbrella: main flow
  keyboard operability). *Completed.*
- AH-0MUBZT64O0056BRY — Reusable in-canvas focus manager (core utility) +
  unit tests. *Completed — the utility this change reuses.*
- AH-0MUBZTFR4001JLF3 — MenuScene keyboard support. *Completed — the
  registration pattern to follow.*
- AH-0MUBZTPDR003A1JT — GameOverScene keyboard support. *Completed.*
- AH-0MUBZUQBL0080B88 — In-game menu keyboard support (PauseScene).
  *Completed.*
- AH-0MUBZTZ7P00838MH — Keyboard-driven scene navigation tests. *Completed.*
- AH-0MU9LRTK3004KR04 / AH-0MUA5GD1D008J6SI / AH-0MUA5I3760044WGQ — ESC
  back-to-menu from the gym index and its tests. *Completed.*
- AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ — Gym index scene. *Completed.*
- AH-0MTHG5BSP006A81R — Gym index discovers all enemy configs. *Completed.*
- AH-0MTV8OV9V002D8B7 — Boss rows grouped in the index. *Completed.*
- AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL — Dev Utilities gym scene / column. *Open — shares the
  same `GymIndex.ts` file.*

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which keyboard-navigation model should the index use — linear
  Tab/arrow cycling, or 2-D grid navigation (left/right between columns,
  up/down within a column)?
  **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION — no operator was available during this
  auto-dispatched intake run. **Assumption taken (documented above):** linear
  cycling via the existing shared `FocusManager`, matching all other scenes in
  the repo. **Recommended (advisory):** linear cycling — smallest, consistent,
  reversible change. If grid navigation is preferred, it should be raised for
  a follow-up work item because it requires extending the shared
  `FocusManager`. Source: repo convention (`src/utils/focusManager.ts`,
  `MenuScene`, `LeaderboardScene`); evidence AH-0MUBZT64O0056BRY.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUA8BGE0006UAU4** – SettingsScene: key-binding remapping + reset to defaults (completed)
- **AH-0MUAYB4EJ005CIYQ** – Power Ups scene title in index page (completed)
- **AH-0MTCO0M3C002Y67S** – GymPowerUps scene wiring (ship, spawn, collect, HUD) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, activate (+285 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+273 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mtv8ov9v002d8b7, ac1, ac4, add, added (+243 more)

# Tests: CSV codec (parse, serialise, coerce, validate)

Create the test suite for the CSV codec module (`src/core/csv.ts`) before implementing the codec itself.

**Context:**

The CSV codec module provides an RFC 4180 CSV parser and serializer that reads flat CSV rows into typed `EnemyConfig` / `ShipConfig` objects. This task creates the **tests** that define the expected behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV parsing — round-trip.** `parseCsvRows` accepts a CSV string (with header row) and returns an array of `Record<string, string>` objects. Each row produces one object; column names come from the header. Empty rows and comment lines (starting with `#`) are skipped.

2. **Type coercion.** `coerceEnemyConfig` converts raw string values to typed fields: numbers parsed via `Number(...)`, enums validated against `EnemyFormationKind` / `EnemyShotPattern`, colours coerced from `0xRRGGBB` hex strings, booleans coerced from `"true"` / `"false"`.

3. **Validation.** Missing required fields produce a validation error. Invalid enum values fall back to defaults. Malformed numbers fall back to `0`. Invalid hex colours fall back to `0x000000`. The validator returns a typed result with errors array (non-destructive).

4. **CSV serialization.** `serializeEnemyConfigs` converts typed `EnemyConfig` objects back to a CSV string with headers in a defined column order. Colours are formatted as `0xRRGGBB`. The output round-trips through `parseCsvRows` → `coerceEnemyConfig`.

5. **RFC 4180 quoting.** Values containing commas, double-quotes, or newlines are properly quoted (enclosed in `""`, with internal `"` escaped as `""`).

6. **Default fallbacks.** When a row has missing columns, `coerceEnemyConfig` fills in sensible defaults from `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` / `DEFAULT_CONFIG` — never returns `undefined` or `NaN`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — test suite for the codec (to be created).
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — type definitions for `EnemyConfig`, enums, and defaults.
- `src/core/config.ts` — type definitions for `ShipConfig` and defaults.

**Dependencies:**

- None (foundation task — must be implemented first).

**Deliverables:**

- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — comprehensive test suite covering all ACs above.
- (The codec implementation in `src/core/csv.ts` will be a separate task.)

# Tests: Config store (in-memory registry, boot load, dev write)

Create the test suite for the config store module (`src/core/configStore.ts`) before implementing the store itself.

**Context:**

The config store provides an in-memory registry that is populated at boot from the committed CSV files. It exposes synchronous `loadEnemyConfig` / `loadShipConfig` accessors. During development, it also supports writes via the Vite plugin endpoint and re-reads.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Boot load.** `loadConfigs()` fetches `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` and `src/data/ship-config.csv` (via HTTP fetch), parses and validates them, and populates the in-memory registry. The registry is ready before the first scene boots.

2. **Sync access.** `loadEnemyConfig(key)` returns the typed `EnemyConfig` from the registry synchronously. `loadShipConfig()` returns the `ShipConfig` synchronously. No async/await required by callers.

3. **Dev write + re-read.** In dev mode, `saveEnemyConfig(config)` writes via PUT to the Vite plugin endpoint, then re-reads the CSV and updates the registry. `saveShipConfig(config)` works the same way.

4. **Production fallback.** In production (static build), writes are disabled. `saveEnemyConfig` / `saveShipConfig` are no-ops that return a status indicating writes are unavailable. The registry is loaded from bundled CSV at build time.

5. **Graceful degradation.** If a CSV fetch fails at boot, the registry falls back to built-in defaults from `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` / `DEFAULT_CONFIG` without throwing. The game still boots.

6. **Key listing and all-configs.** `listEnemyConfigKeys()` and `loadAllEnemyConfigs()` serve from the registry, returning the same data shapes as the current implementation.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — test suite (to be created).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — config store module (to be created).
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — type definitions and defaults.
- `src/core/config.ts` — type definitions and defaults.

**Dependencies:**

- None (foundation task — must be implemented first).

- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — comprehensive test suite covering all ACs above.

# Config store: in-memory registry, boot load, dev write

Implement the config store module that provides the in-memory registry serving typed configs from CSV.

**Context:**

The config store (`src/core/configStore.ts`) replaces localStorage as the persistence layer. It fetches CSVs at boot, parses them using the CSV codec, and serves them synchronously. In dev mode, it supports writes via the Vite plugin endpoint.

# Tests: Vite CSV plugin (GET/PUT, atomic write, validation)

Create the test suite for the Vite CSV plugin before implementing the plugin itself.

**Context:**

The Vite plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`) exposes dev-server middleware endpoints for reading and writing CSV files. It runs only in dev mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **GET endpoint.** `GET /api/csv/src/data/enemy-configs.csv` returns the file contents with `Content-Type: text/csv`. The path is resolved relative to the project root.

2. **PUT endpoint (upsert).** `PUT /api/csv/src/data/enemy-configs.csv` with a CSV body validates the row, finds the matching key, and overwrites that row. The file is written atomically (temp file + rename).

3. **PUT endpoint (append for Save As).** `PUT` with a new key appends a new row. Duplicate keys are rejected with a 409 status.

4. **Validation.** Invalid CSV rows are rejected with a 400 status and a human-readable error message. The file is not modified on validation failure.

5. **Dev-only.** The plugin only registers when `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` or `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. In production builds, it is a no-op.

6. **Atomic write.** The file is written via a temp file in the same directory, then renamed. If the write fails mid-way, the original file is untouched.

**Key Files:**

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — test suite (to be created).
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — plugin module (to be created).

**Dependencies:**

- None for test file creation. Plugin implementation is a sibling task.

**Deliverables:**

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — comprehensive test suite covering all ACs above.

# Vite CSV plugin: dev middleware (GET/PUT, atomic write, validation)

Implement the Vite dev-server middleware plugin that exposes CSV read/write endpoints.

**Context:**

The plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`) registers GET and PUT handlers during development. It uses the CSV codec for validation and performs atomic writes via temp file + rename.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **GET handler.** Serves CSV files from `src/data/` with correct `Content-Type: text/csv`. Returns 404 for unknown paths.

2. **PUT handler — upsert.** Receives a CSV body, parses and validates it, finds the matching row by key, and overwrites it. Returns 200 with the updated row data.

3. **PUT handler — append (Save As).** When the key does not exist, appends a new row. Returns 201 (created) with the new row data.

4. **Validation errors.** Returns 400 with a JSON error object describing which fields are invalid. The file is not modified.

5. **Duplicate key rejection.** Returns 409 (Conflict) if Save As attempts to add a row with an existing key.

6. **Atomic write.** Uses `fs.writeFileSync` to a temp file (e.g., `.tmp_{filename}`), then `fs.renameSync` to replace the original. If rename fails, the original file is preserved.

7. **Dev-only registration.** The plugin only registers its middleware when Vite is running in dev mode (`server.mode === 'development'`).

8. **Registered in vite.config.ts.** The plugin is imported and added to the `plugins` array in `vite.config.ts`.

**Key Files:**

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — new plugin module (to be created).
- `./vite.config.ts` — updated to register the plugin.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — CSV codec for validation.

**Dependencies:**

- `src/core/csv.ts` — the CSV codec module (for validation during PUT).
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — tests for the plugin (sibling task).

**Deliverables:**

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the Vite plugin implementation.
- Updated `vite.config.ts` — includes `configCsvPlugin` in the plugins array.

# Wire up: config loaders, gym Save/SaveAs, discovery

Rewire `loadEnemyConfig`, `loadShipConfig`, and related functions to use the CSV-backed store. Update the gym scenes to use the store's Save/SaveAs path. Update discovery and constants re-exports.

**Context:**

This task connects all the pieces: the config store replaces localStorage in the existing config modules, and the gym scenes are updated to use the CSV write path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Rewire `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`.** `loadEnemyConfig(key)` delegates to `configStore.loadEnemyConfig(key)`. `saveEnemyConfig(config)` delegates to `configStore.saveEnemyConfig(config)` (dev write) and returns a status. `listEnemyConfigKeys()` and `loadAllEnemyConfigs()` serve from the registry. `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` is still exported for fallback defaults but is no longer the primary data source.

2. **Rewire `src/core/config.ts`.** `loadShipConfig()` delegates to `configStore.loadShipConfig()`. `saveShipConfig(config)` delegates to `configStore.saveShipConfig(config)`. `DEFAULT_CONFIG` is still exported for fallback defaults.

3. **GymEnemies Save/SaveAs.** `GymEnemies.ts` uses the store's save path (HTTP PUT via the Vite plugin) instead of writing to localStorage. Save overwrites the active enemy; Save As appends a new row with key sanitisation and duplicate rejection. On success, the scene re-reads the config and reflects changes.

4. **GymPlayer Save.** `GymPlayer.ts` uses the store's save path for the ship config instead of writing to localStorage.

5. **Enemy gym discovery.** `src/utils/enemyGymDiscovery.ts` uses `listEnemyConfigKeys()` / `loadAllEnemyConfigs()` from the store (same API shape, no changes to callers).

6. **Constants re-exports.** `src/core/constants.ts` re-exports are updated to be lazy (function-based) or boot-time synced. If `loadConfigs()` has not yet run, they fall back to `DEFAULT_CONFIG` values.

7. **No localStorage usage.** The config modules no longer read or write localStorage directly.

Create integration tests that verify the complete flow from CSV file through boot loading, gym Save/SaveAs, and re-read.

# CSV codec: RFC 4180 parser, serialiser, typed coercion, validation

Implement the CSV codec module (`src/core/csv.ts`) that parses flat CSV rows into typed `EnemyConfig` / `ShipConfig` objects and serialises them back.

**Context:**

The codec is the foundation of the CSV-based configuration system. It is used by the boot loader (to parse committed CSVs), the Vite plugin (to validate writes), and the config store (to re-read after writes). It must be dependency-free and hand-rolled (no new runtime dependencies).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parser.** `parseCsvRows(csv: string): Record<string, string>[]` parses an RFC 4180 CSV string with a header row into an array of objects. Empty rows and comment lines (starting with `#`) are skipped. A leading BOM (U+FEFF) is stripped.

2. **Serialiser.** `serializeEnemyConfigs(configs: EnemyConfig[]): string` and `serializeShipConfig(config: ShipConfig): string` produce a CSV string with a header row and one row per config. Output round-trips through `parseCsvRows` → coercion. Colours are formatted as `0xRRGGBB`.

3. **RFC 4180 quoting.** Fields containing commas, double-quotes, or newlines are wrapped in double quotes, with internal quotes escaped as `""`. The parser reverses this correctly.

4. **Typed coercion.** `coerceEnemyConfig(row, defaults)` and `coerceShipConfig(row, defaults)` convert raw string values to typed fields: numbers via `Number(...)`, enums validated against `EnemyFormationKind` / `EnemyShotPattern` / `ControlScheme`, colours via `parseInt(value, 16)`.

5. **Validation.** A validator returns a typed result `{ ok: boolean; errors: string[] }`. Missing required fields, malformed numbers, invalid enums, and invalid hex colours are reported. Coercion falls back to `defaults` for every invalid field — never produces `undefined`, `NaN`, or an invalid enum.

6. **Column mapping.** A documented, stable column order per config type (exported as constants) maps CSV headers to typed fields. Unknown headers are ignored; missing headers fall back to defaults.

7. **No runtime dependencies.** The codec uses only the TypeScript/JavaScript standard library.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/csv.ts` — new codec module (to be created).
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — `EnemyConfig`, enums, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS`.
- `src/core/config.ts` — `ShipConfig`, `ControlScheme`, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.

**Dependencies:**

- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — the codec test suite (created by the sibling "Tests: CSV codec" task; implementation must make those tests pass).

**Deliverables:**

- `src/core/csv.ts` — the CSV codec implementation.
- Exported column-order constants for enemy and ship configs.

# Leaderboard entry screen should show position in table

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** medium

> **Original request (preserved):** "When entering a high score into the
> leaderboard the leaderboard display the position of the players score in the
> leaderboard, filling in the initials as they are typed. Highlight that line
> somehow."

## Problem statement

On game over, a qualifying player types their three initials but receives no
feedback about where their score will land until they submit and return to the
menu. The ranked table on the game-over screen stays static, so the player
cannot tell whether the run is about to rank #1 or #10.

## Users

- An arcade player who has just finished a run and is entering their initials on
  the game-over screen.

  > **User story:** As a player entering my initials after a high score, I want
  > to see my score inserted into the leaderboard at the position it will take,
  > with my initials filling in live and my row highlighted, so that I know how
  > well I did before I commit.

## Existing state

- `GameOverScene` (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`) renders a static leaderboard
  via `renderLeaderboard` (`src/ui/leaderboardView.ts`) and prompts for
  3-letter initials using the shared `FocusManager`.
- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` owns persistence and ranking
  (`getEntries`, `addEntry`, `isQualifying`, `MAX_ENTRIES = 10`); `rank` is
  recomputed on read and never trusted from storage.
- Keystrokes currently update only the initials field text; the table is not
  re-rendered, and there is no marker for the player's prospective position.
- `LeaderboardScene` (main menu) renders the same table through the shared
  helper and must remain unchanged.

## Desired change

While a **qualifying** score is being entered on the game-over screen:

1. Compute the prospective entry's rank from the current table and the final
   score.
2. Show the player's row at that rank **immediately on screen open**, with
   initials rendered as placeholders until typing begins (Q2 answer:
   immediately).
3. Fill in the initials live as they are typed and update the row on every A–Z
   key and Backspace.
4. Highlight the player's row with a distinct colour plus a leading marker
   (Q1 answer: option A).
5. When the table already holds 10 entries, insert the prospective row at its
   true rank and drop the current lowest entry, so at most 10 rows are shown
   (Q3 answer: insert and drop).
6. On submit, the persisted entry occupies the same rank the preview showed.
7. Non-qualifying scores show no prospective row (explanatory message
   unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Live prospective row shown immediately:** For a qualifying score,
  the game-over leaderboard shows exactly one row representing the player's
  prospective entry as soon as the screen opens, at the rank it will occupy.
  The row's initials render as placeholders until typing begins.
- [ ] **AC2 — Live initials:** Each A–Z key press and Backspace updates that
  row's initials immediately (typed letters shown, unfilled slots rendered as
  placeholders), before any submit.
- [ ] **AC3 — Highlight:** The prospective row is visually distinguishable from
  every other row by a distinct colour plus a leading marker (e.g. `▶`).
- [ ] **AC4 — Correct placement and cap:** The prospective row is inserted by
  score descending with the same stable tie-break as `Leaderboard.addEntry`;
  the table never shows more than `MAX_ENTRIES` (10) rows, and when full the
  current lowest entry is displaced.
- [ ] **AC5 — Qualifying only:** Non-qualifying scores render no prospective
  row and write nothing to storage.
- [ ] **AC6 — Submit consistency:** After submit, the persisted entry occupies
  the same rank shown by the preview.
- [ ] **AC7 — Regression:** `LeaderboardScene` (main-menu table) is unchanged
  and existing GameOverScene/Leaderboard tests continue to pass.
- [ ] **AC8 — Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover rank insertion
  (including equal-score ties and full-table displacement), immediate preview
  visibility before typing, live initials update, highlight marker/colour,
  Backspace-to-empty, and non-qualifying behaviour.
- [ ] **AC9 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries.
- [ ] **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Keyboard-only entry through `FocusManager` is retained; no on-screen
  keyboard is added.
- Reuse `src/ui/leaderboardView.ts` for rendering where practical so the
  game-over and main-menu tables stay consistent.
- `Leaderboard.ts` remains the single owner of ranking and persistence; a pure,
  testable helper for the prospective rank is preferred over duplicating sort
  logic in the scene.
- No new dependencies.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the prospective rank uses the same stable tie-break as
  `addEntry` — a new equal score ranks after existing equal-score entries.
- **Assumption:** the prospective row's date column shows today's ISO date
  (`todayISO()`), matching the eventual persisted entry.
- **Assumption:** highlighting applies only to the game-over entry screen; the
  main-menu `LeaderboardScene` table is unchanged.
- **Risk (scope creep):** extra polish (animation, sound, online leaderboard)
  is recorded as separate linked work items, not added to this scope.
- **Risk:** re-rendering rows on each keystroke could leak text objects; the
  implementation should destroy/replace preview rows rather than accumulate
  them.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` — add a pure helper to compute the prospective
  ranked preview (reusing the existing `sortAndRank` semantics).
- `src/ui/leaderboardView.ts` — support a highlighted/preview row in
  `renderLeaderboard` (or a sibling helper).
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — render and refresh the prospective row on
  initials changes.
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` — tests for the preview behaviour.
- `src/ui/leaderboardView.test.ts` (new if no existing coverage) — tests for
  highlighted/preview row formatting.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §5 — document the live preview-row UX.
- `README.md` §Leaderboard — update the game-over description.

## Related work

- **Implement game-over qualifying, date and full leaderboard (AH-0MUD9ZOM4001LACR)**
  (completed) — built the game-over table this feature extends.
- **Test: Game-over leaderboard UX (AH-0MUD9ZNN30065ZLP)** (completed) —
  existing test coverage for the game-over leaderboard flow.
- **Keyboard entry / `FocusManager` work (AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9)** (completed) —
  initials-entry focus model reused here.
- **Implement GameOverScene — scoring, lives, game-over flow
  (AH-0MU731426003FE71)** (completed) — scene this feature modifies.
- **Implement Leaderboard persistence module (AH-0MUD9ZOAR0099DJZ)** (completed)
  — ranking API used for placement.
- **Docs: GDD and README leaderboard updates (AH-0MUD9ZP94006OYL4)**
  (completed) — docs to amend.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL** – Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (open)
- **AH-0MT7URFNN004Z01L** – Remove combo bonus from GDD and clarify lives model (completed)
- **AH-0MT7UTPH3001B6IE** – Settle engine selection on Phaser - remove engine options B and C from GDD (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, add (+265 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+239 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac4, add, added, animation (+201 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Highlight treatment.** How should the player's prospective row be
  highlighted? Options: A) distinct colour plus a leading marker (e.g. `▶`);
  B) blinking/pulsing row; C) background panel behind the row; D) other.
  **Recommended:** A. — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "A".
- **Q2 — Preview visibility before typing.** Should the prospective row be
  visible immediately when a qualifying game-over screen opens (initials shown
  as placeholders), or only after the first letter is typed?
  **Recommended:** visible immediately. — **Answer (producer, interactive
  reply):** "immediately".
- **Q3 — Full-table behaviour.** When the table already holds 10 entries and
  the score qualifies, should the preview insert at its true rank and drop the
  current lowest entry (keeping 10 rows), or temporarily show an 11th row?
  **Recommended:** drop the lowest. — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):**
  "insert and drop".

# Allow `v*` release tags to deploy to the `github-pages` environment (reproducible policy + docs)

## Problem statement

`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` triggers on `v*` tag pushes, but the repository's `github-pages` environment has a custom deployment branch policy that allows only the `dev` branch. Every release tag is therefore rejected by environment protection, so the Pages deploy fails, the failed check run lands on the release-branch HEAD, and the ship release wrapper's `waitForPRMerge()` always falls back to a manual merge.

## Users

- **Operator (release runner):** runs the ship release and expects it to auto-merge and publish without the manual-merge fallback.
- **Player:** expects each release to be live and playable at `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/`.
- **Future maintainer:** sets up or recovers the repository and needs a reproducible, documented way to configure the Pages environment policy.

### Example user stories

- As a release runner, I want pushing a `v*` release tag to deploy to GitHub Pages without environment-protection rejection, so that the release PR's checks pass and the ship wrapper merges the PR automatically.
- As a future maintainer, I want a documented, idempotent script that configures the `github-pages` environment deployment policy, so I do not have to rediscover the `dev`-only policy failure.
- As a player, I want every release to be published automatically at the project Pages URL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Tag policy present.** The `github-pages` environment has a deployment policy for tags matching `v*`, in addition to the existing `dev` branch policy. Verify: `gh api repos/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies --jq '.branch_policies[] | "\(.type):\(.name)"'` outputs both `branch:dev` and `tag:v*`.
- **Reproducible, idempotent setup script.** `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` exists, is executable, adds the `v*` tag policy only when missing, and is safe to re-run (second run makes no change and exits 0). It fails loudly with a clear message when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated. Verify: `bash -n` syntax check plus running it twice and inspecting the API result.
- **Deploy succeeds end to end.** Re-running workflow run `35993333739` (tag `v0.1.5`) completes with both the `build` and `deploy` jobs `success`, and `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/` serves the game. Verify: `gh run view 35993333739 --json conclusion,jobs` and an HTTP request to the Pages URL.
- **Tag-only trigger preserved.** `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy. Verify: workflow YAML inspected and unchanged.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Only a `v*` tag policy may be added; the existing `dev` branch policy must be preserved.
- The workflow's tag-only trigger semantics must not change (superseding Github Hosted Alpha (`AH-0MU9P20Q2003D2V0`) AC5 is out of scope).
- The fix must live in this repository plus the GitHub repository setting; the global ship skill must not be edited (out of repository scope).
- Applying the setting requires a `gh` token with repository admin; if unavailable, the operator applies it manually and the script/documentation records the requirement.

## Existing state

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` triggers on `push` of tags matching `v*`; the `deploy` job targets environment `github-pages`.
- Environment `github-pages` has `custom_branch_policies: true` with exactly one policy: `branch:dev`. No tag policy exists.
- Release flow (`merge-dev-to-main.sh`) tags `vX.Y.Z` on the release merge commit, pushes the tag and the release branch, then opens the PR to `main`. The tag push triggers the deploy, whose rejection leaves a failed check on the release-branch HEAD, blocking `run-release.js`'s `waitForPRMerge()`.
- Evidence: workflow run `35993333739` (`event: push`, `headBranch: v0.1.5`) — `build` succeeded, `deploy` failed with zero steps (environment protection rejection).
- No `scripts/` directory exists and README has no deployment/Pages configuration section.

## Desired change

- Add a `tag:v*` deployment policy to the `github-pages` environment (keeping `branch:dev`).
- Add an idempotent, documented setup script that applies and verifies the policy via `gh api`.
- Document the environment policy requirement and the script in README.
- Verify by re-running the failed workflow run so the release tag deploys successfully.

## Key Files

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` — New idempotent script that adds/verifies the `v*` tag deployment policy on the `github-pages` environment via `gh api`.
- `README.md` — New deployment subsection documenting the `github-pages` environment policy requirement and script usage.
- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` — No change expected; tag-only trigger retained and verified.
- GitHub repository setting — `github-pages` environment deployment policy (applied by the script, verified via `gh api`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The `gh` token has repository-admin rights to modify environment policies; otherwise the operator applies the policy manually and the script reports the required command.
- **Risk:** The environment protection rule is the sole cause of the failure. Mitigation: re-run the workflow and confirm `deploy` succeeds; inspect `gh api .../pages` if it still fails.
- **Risk:** `gh run rerun 35993333739` may be disallowed or the run may be too old. Mitigation: fall back to pushing a fresh `v*` tag through the normal release flow.
- **Risk:** Wildcard tag policy (`v*`) may not be accepted by the API. Mitigation: verify with a GET after POST and adjust the pattern if needed.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Hardening the ship wrapper to ignore non-required checks (the original Option C) is out of scope for this repository and would be a separate work item in the agent-framework repo.

## Related work

- Github Hosted Alpha (`AH-0MU9P20Q2003D2V0`) — completed feature that introduced the tag-triggered Pages workflow; its AC5 requires that non-tag events do not deploy.
- discovered-from:AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T.
- Discord notification fails: projectRoot is not defined (`AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ`) — completed; unrelated ship notification path.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB** – ship producer-review gate remediation hint uses wrong wl flag casing (open)
- **AH-0MTAFH1ZF003EGDF** – Add ship deceleration when no inputs, with slider to control deceleration rate (completed)
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: actually, add, allowed, alongside, blocking (+53 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: add, allowed, blocking, branch, build (+37 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: actually, add, alongside, branch, build (+35 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Which fix approach should this item implement?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-24): Option A — add a `v*` tag deployment policy to the `github-pages` environment (alongside the existing `dev` branch policy). Research: confirmed the environment currently has a single `branch:dev` policy and that the tag-triggered deploy is rejected before any step runs.
- **Q2: Should the item also add documentation of the required environment policy and a reproducible script?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-24): Yes — update the documentation and add a reproducible script.

## Plan

**Planned:** 2026-09-24T21:48:32Z (plan skill, agent Map)

Feature breakdown (test-first ordering, vertical slices):

1. Add Pages deploy trigger regression test (`AH-0MUG2CG4Y000LDYF`) — task, covers AC4. No dependencies.
2. Add idempotent Pages environment setup script (`AH-0MUG2CGIQ002Y63K`) — task, covers AC2 and AC6. No dependencies.
3. Apply tag policy and verify deploy (`AH-0MUG2CGVM004JM6Q`) — task, covers AC1 and AC3. Depends on #2.
4. Document Pages environment policy (`AH-0MUG2CH90002U325`) — docs, covers AC5. Depends on #2.

- `AH-0MUG2CGVM004JM6Q` depends on `AH-0MUG2CGIQ002Y63K`

Decision: full planning performed (effort Small, risk Medium). The approval gate was not triggered (effort below Medium and risk below High), so the plan proceeded straight to automated review.

# Add Pages deploy trigger regression test

## Summary

Test-first verifier feature for *GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev)* (`AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77`). Adds an automated regression test that pins the **tag-only trigger contract** of `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`, so a future workflow edit cannot silently start deploying on branch pushes or pull requests.

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want an automated test that fails if the Pages deploy workflow starts triggering on non-tag events, so the tag-only release contract is protected without manual YAML review.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC4** requires that `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes, and that non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The workflow currently declares `on.push.tags: ['v*']` and a `deploy` job targeting environment `github-pages`.
- This item is created and completed **before** the environment-policy implementation items (test-first ordering).

## Scope

In scope:

- A hermetic vitest test that reads `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` from the repository root and asserts its trigger shape.

Out of scope:

- Changing the workflow (no change is expected for this fix).
- Calling the live GitHub API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The test asserts the only trigger is `push` with `tags: ['v*']` — no `branches`, no `pull_request`, and no `workflow_dispatch`.
- The test asserts the workflow contains a `deploy` job targeting the `github-pages` environment and a `build` job the deploy needs.
- The test is hermetic (reads only the checked-out workflow file) and runs as part of `npm test` with no new runtime dependency (`npm run build` and `npm test` both pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a vitest test (e.g. `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts`, or co-located under `src/` if `scripts/` has no test wiring) that reads the workflow file using `node:fs` relative to the repo root.
- Parse the workflow text with focused assertions (regex/string checks or `yaml` if already available transitively); avoid adding a production dependency for a single test.
- Assert: `push.tags` is exactly `['v*']`; no `push.branches`; no `pull_request` / `workflow_dispatch` trigger keys; `jobs.deploy.environment.name == 'github-pages'`.
- Confirm the test is picked up by the existing `vitest.config.ts` include globs; adjust the include pattern only if the file lives outside the current test roots.

## Deliverables

- New automated trigger-contract test.
- `npm test` green including the new test.

## Dependencies

# Add idempotent Pages environment setup script

## Summary

Adds a reproducible, executable `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` that adds the `tag:v*` deployment policy to the `github-pages` environment via `gh api`, only when it is missing, and never removes the existing `dev` branch policy. Ships with automated tests (test-first inside the item).

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want a documented, idempotent script that configures the `github-pages` environment deployment policy, so I do not have to rediscover the `dev`-only policy failure that blocked every `v*` release tag.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC2** requires `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` to exist, be executable, add the `v*` tag policy only when missing, be safe to re-run (second run makes no change, exits 0), and fail loudly when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated.
- There is currently **no** `scripts/` directory in the repository.
- The live environment already has exactly one policy: `branch:dev`. The script must preserve it.

## Scope

In scope:

- The setup script and its hermetic tests.

Out of scope:

- Applying the policy to the live repository (see *Apply tag policy and verify deploy*), and README documentation (see *Document Pages environment policy*).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` exists, is executable, adds the `v*` tag policy only when missing, and is safe to re-run (second run makes no change and exits 0).
- The script preserves the existing `dev` branch policy and adds only a `tag:v*` policy (never deletes or rewrites existing policies).
- It fails loudly with a clear, actionable message when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated (non-zero exit, no partial writes).
- Automated tests cover add-once, idempotent second run, dev-policy preservation, and fail-loud-without-`gh`/auth, using a stubbed `gh` on `PATH` (no live API calls).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`bash -n` syntax check, `npm test`, and `npm run build` all pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Script: accept an optional `--repo <owner/name>` (default: resolve from the current clone via `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`). Preflight `command -v gh` and `gh auth status`; exit non-zero with an actionable message otherwise.
- Read existing policies with `gh api repos/$REPO/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies`; if a policy with `type == "tag"` and `name == "v*"` is present, print "already configured" and exit 0 without any write.
- Otherwise `POST` `{"name":"v*","type":"tag"}` to the same endpoint, then `GET` again to verify the policy is present (fail loudly if verification fails).
- Tests: create a temp `gh` stub executable that logs argv and returns canned JSON, prepend its directory to `PATH`, run the script with `bash`, and assert the recorded calls (no POST on second run; POST payload on first run; `dev` never deleted) plus exit codes. Keep all tests hermetic.

## Deliverables

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` (executable).
- Hermetic script tests wired into `npm test`.
- Green `npm test` / `npm run build`.

## Dependencies

None (sequenced after *Add Pages deploy trigger regression test*).

## Key Files

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` — New idempotent script that adds/verifies the `v*` tag deployment policy on the `github-pages` environment via `gh api`.
- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts` — New hermetic tests using a stubbed `gh`.
- `vitest.config.ts` — Test include globs; may need to cover `scripts/`.

# Implement — AsteroidSpawner (pure planner)

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Create `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — a pure (no Phaser dependency) planner module that computes when and where asteroids should spawn based on the global wave index.

## Module Structure

### Exported types

```typescript
export interface SpawnEvent {
  sizeTier: 'large' | 'medium';
  x: number;
  y: number;
  vx: number;
  vy: number;
}
```

### Exported function

```typescript
export function computeSpawns(
  globalWaveIndex: number,
  gameWidth: number,
  gameHeight: number,
  waveTimeLimit: number,
  rng: () => number,
): SpawnEvent[];
```

## Algorithm (per spec)

### 1. Per-wave count

Start at 2. Every time the large weight reaches the reset threshold, double: `2 → 4 → 8 → …`.

### 2. Size weighting

- Medium weight fixed at 80.
- Large weight starts at 20 and increases by +20 per wave.
- When large weight reaches 2 × medium (160), reset to 80:20 and double the count.

Formula: `largeWeight = min(20 + 20 * (globalWaveIndex % wavesPerReset), 160)` where `wavesPerReset` depends on when the reset threshold is hit.

### 3. Spawn timing

- Divide the wave into N equal segments (N = count).
- Anchor for asteroid i is `i / N`.
- Apply ±5% jitter, clamped to [0, 0.95].
- First asteroid constrained to first 10% of wave.
- Times must be ordered and non-duplicated.

### 4. Offscreen edge + velocity

- Choose random edge uniformly (top/bottom/left/right).
- Place asteroid at random point along that edge, offset outward by `halfSize + margin` so fully outside viewport.
- Give inward-directed velocity: perpendicular to spawn edge with ±30° spread, at the tier's canonical speed.
- The inward component must dominate so it enters the playfield promptly.

### 5. Tuning constants (exported for easy retuning)

```typescript
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_BASE_COUNT = 2;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_BASE_LARGE_WEIGHT = 20;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_MEDIUM_WEIGHT = 80;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_LARGE_WEIGHT_INCREMENT = 20;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_LARGE_WEIGHT_RESET = 160;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_JITTER_FRACTION = 0.05;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_MAX_JITTER_FRACTION = 0.95;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_FIRST_ASTEROID_MAX_FRACTION = 0.10;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_INWARD_ANGULAR_SPREAD = Math.PI / 6; // ±30°
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_OUTWARD_MARGIN = 10; // px beyond half-size
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- `computeSpawns` returns exactly `count` events for any `globalWaveIndex >= 0`.
- Spawn count starts at 2 for `globalWaveIndex` 0–6, doubles at 7 (4), consistent with weight escalation.
- Large weight increases by +20 per wave; resets when it reaches 2× medium weight (160).
- First spawn time fraction is ≤ 0.10; subsequent times are spread across the wave with jitter.
- All spawn positions are fully offscreen (distance from viewport ≥ asteroid half-size + margin).
- All velocity vectors have inward components (toward the viewport centre).
- Output is deterministic for a given `globalWaveIndex`, dimensions, and RNG sequence.
- No Phaser runtime dependencies — pure TypeScript functions only.

- Covers parent AC2 — A wave begins with 2 asteroids by default; every spawned asteroid appears **offscreen** (fully outside the viewport on a random edge) and drifts inward into the playfield.
- Covers parent AC3 — Spawn timing: the first asteroid spawns within the first 10 % of the wave window and the second around 50 %; for higher counts spawn times are spread across the wave with randomised jitter and remain ordered/non-duplicated.
- Covers parent AC4 — Size weighting: asteroids are large or medium, weighted toward medium (baseline 80:20). The large weight increases by +20 each wave; when it reaches 2× the medium weight, weights reset to 80:20 and the per-wave count doubles (2 → 4 → 8 → …).

## Key Files

- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — new module

# Implement — PlayScene asteroid spawner integration

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Integrate `AsteroidSpawner` into `PlayScene.tick(dt)` so asteroids spawn at computed times during regular waves.

## Changes to PlayScene

### 1. Spawner state

Track planned spawns for the current wave:
```typescript
private pendingAsteroidSpawns: SpawnEvent[] = [];
private asteroidsSpawnedThisWave = 0;
```

### 2. Wave start — plan spawns

At the start of each regular wave (when `beginGame()` is called or when `onEnemyDestroyed()` returns `waveCleared` / `levelCleared`):

```typescript
private planAsteroidSpawns(): void {
  const wm = this.waveManager;
  if (!wm.currentWave() || wm.bossTriggered || wm.bossActive || wm.bossDefeated) {
    this.pendingAsteroidSpawns = [];
    this.asteroidsSpawnedThisWave = 0;
    return;
  }
  this.pendingAsteroidSpawns = computeSpawns(
    wm.globalWaveIndex,
    GAME_WIDTH,
    GAME_HEIGHT,
    WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS,
    this.rng,
  );
  this.asteroidsSpawnedThisWave = 0;
}
```

### 3. Tick loop — release due spawns

In `tick(dt)`, after the wave timer increments:

```typescript
// Asteroid spawner — release any due spawns
while (
  this.asteroidsSpawnedThisWave < this.pendingAsteroidSpawns.length
) {
  const next = this.pendingAsteroidSpawns[this.asteroidsSpawnedThisWave];
  const spawnTime = next.x * WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS; // reusing x as time fraction...
  // Actually: computeSpawns returns SpawnEvent with time info
  // Release when elapsed >= spawnTime
  break;
}
```

Actually, the spawn time needs to be stored in the SpawnEvent. Let me refine: the `SpawnEvent` already has timing info embedded. The scene checks: `if (waveElapsed >= spawnTimeFraction * WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS)` then spawn.

### 4. Spawn execution

When a spawn is due:
1. Call `scene.spawnAsteroidAt(event.x, event.y, event.vx, event.vy)` — or add a new helper that accepts velocity.
2. Register the spawn with `WaveManager.registerDynamicSpawn(1)`.
3. Increment `asteroidsSpawnedThisWave`.

### 5. Pause / transition / boss exclusion

Skip asteroid spawning when:
- `transitionTimer > 0` (during transitions)
- `this.paused` (scene is paused)
- `bossTriggered` or `bossActive` (boss encounter)

### 6. Wave start hook

Call `planAsteroidSpawns()` whenever a new regular wave begins:
- After `beginGame()`
- After `onEnemyDestroyed()` returns `waveCleared`
- After `onEnemyDestroyed()` returns `levelCleared`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Asteroids spawn at the correct times during each wave (verified by tick-driven test).
- Spawned asteroids are registered with WaveManager as dynamic spawns.
- No asteroids spawn during boss encounters.
- No asteroids spawn during transitions or when paused.
- Existing asteroid behaviours (splitting, timeout survival, transition collidability, boss-entry cleanup) are preserved.
- The spawner uses the scene's injectable `rng` for determinism.

- Covers parent AC1 — Every regular wave of every level (Levels 1–5) spawns asteroids from the random offscreen spawner; the boss encounter spawns none.
- Covers parent AC5 — Spawned asteroids are registered with `WaveManager` as dynamic spawns so wave-clear accounting includes them, and existing asteroid behaviours (splitting, timeout survival, transition collidability, boss-entry cleanup) are preserved.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — integrate spawner into tick loop

# Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview

## Context

The runtime auto-sequencer (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is fully implemented but not wired into the game. There is no way for designers or testers to interact with it visually. This work item creates a gym scene that provides a hands-on interface for designing and previewing difficulty curves.

discovered-from:AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X

## Goal

Add a new **Dev Utilities** category/section to the gym index, and create a gym scene within it that provides:

1. **Curve editor** — an interactive way to define the target difficulty curve (array of scores, one per wave)
2. **Regenerate button** — when clicked, runs the sequencer against the current curve and displays the resulting waves
3. **Wave list** — shows each generated wave with its enemy composition, target difficulty, and the resulting wave
4. **Edit-to-clear behaviour** — if the curve is edited, the wave list is cleared and replaced with an instruction to click the regenerate button

## Scope

- Add a **Dev Utilities** column/section to the gym index (GymIndex.ts) — follows the same pattern as the existing ENEMIES and Bosses columns
- Create src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts (and its test file)
- The scene uses the existing sequencer() from difficultySequencer.ts
- Plain-DOM tuning panel overlay (same pattern as GymPlayer) for the curve editor
- Phaser canvas for the wave list display (Phaser text objects)

## Curve editor design

- Each wave in the curve is represented as a row with:
  - A numeric slider (0–100) for the target difficulty
  - A Remove button to delete that wave row
- An "Add Wave" button to append a new wave row at the end
- The "Regenerate" button runs the sequencer and populates the wave list below
- When the curve is edited (any slider moved, wave added/removed), the wave list is cleared and replaced with instruction text: "Edit made — click Regenerate to preview"

## Wave list display

- Each wave entry shows:
  - Wave number
  - Target difficulty
  - Enemy composition (enemy type, count)
  - Whether shooting is enabled
- Entries rendered as Phaser text objects, ordered top-to-bottom

## Non-goals

- Saving/loading curves (could be added later)
- Visual preview of enemy formations (text-only for now)
- Drag-to-reorder waves in the curve editor

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Gym index shows a "Dev Utilities" section** — a new column or section in the gym index listing gym scenes under the Dev Utilities category
2. **GymCurveSequencer scene is listed** under the Dev Utilities section and can be launched from the gym index
3. **Curve editor works** — user can add wave rows, remove wave rows, and adjust target difficulty via sliders (0–100)
4. **Regenerate button** — clicking it runs sequencer() with the current curve and candidate pool, populating the wave list
5. **Wave list is cleared on curve edit** — when the user edits the curve (any change), the wave list is replaced with instruction text to click regenerate
6. **Wave entries display correctly** — each shows wave number, target difficulty, enemy composition, and shooting status
7. **Back to index button** works (arrow-left INDEX)
8. **ESC returns to main menu** (consistent with other gym scenes)
9. **All tests pass** — the scene has unit tests verifying the curve editor and regenerate flow

## Revision — audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the first implementation with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. Make the wave description a table, with column headings. Provide a help box in the bottom right summarizing each column.

Additional acceptance criteria:

10. **Wave preview is a table** — the wave preview renders a table with column headings (Wave, Target, Composition, Shooting) and one aligned row per wave.
11. **Column guide help box** — a help box anchored to the bottom-right of the canvas summarises each wave-table column.

## Revision — second audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the implementation again with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. The UI works, but the generated levels are not good. Firstly, why do we have an actual and error value? Why don't we just create as close the target as possible? Secondly, the higher levels seem to just repeat the phaser with shooting.

Root cause confirmed by reproducing the sequencer output: `sequencer()` picked exactly one candidate group per wave and a single group's `enemyDifficulty` score saturates around 33 (e.g. `phaser×12`), so every target at or above ~40 produced the identical `phaser×12` wave — hence the large error values and the repetition.

Revised acceptance criteria:

12. **Wave generation reaches the target** — the preview table no longer shows redundant ACTUAL/ERROR columns; the table columns are WAVE / TARGET / COMPOSITION / SHOOTING. The sequencer composes a wave from one or more candidate groups so the wave's summed difficulty is within a small tolerance of the target for every target above the old single-group ceiling (previously capped at ~33) up to 100.
13. **Higher waves are varied** — waves with different (especially higher) targets produce meaningfully different enemy compositions instead of every high wave repeating the same archetype (e.g. `phaser` with shooting).

## Key Files

- src/scenes/GymIndex.ts — add Dev Utilities section
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts — new scene
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.test.ts — tests for the scene
- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts — sequencer (extended to compose multi-group waves)
- src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts — existing scorer (read-only)
- src/core/enemyConfig.ts — existing enemy configs for candidate pool
- src/utils/gymNavigation.ts — shared back-to-index navigation
- src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts — gym scene auto-discovery (no changes needed, scene auto-appears)

# Intake brief — Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md

**Headline:** The producer directive that gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the game is currently implicit in the architecture notes but never stated as a rule; this item adds an explicit, discoverable gym-parity principle to the repo-local `AGENTS.md` so future agents and contributors apply gameplay changes consistently across the gyms and the game.

## Problem statement

Operators repeatedly see behaviour drift between the gym scenes and the shipped game. The producer's directive is that gyms and the game must execute the same core code, and that gym behaviours are the parity reference. That principle is **not stated as a rule** in the repo-local `AGENTS.md`, so it is easy for a contributor to change gameplay in one scene without updating the corresponding gym(s) — or vice versa — without violating any documented rule.

Verification performed: `grep -ni 'gym\|parity\|reference' AGENTS.md` returns no gym-parity rule (only generic workflow/documentation references). The `AGENTS.md` "Architecture Notes for Agents" section does describe the shared combat core and states that "no production scene keeps a divergent copy", but it does not state a general gym-parity rule or name the gym directories it applies to.

## Users

- **As an agent/contributor**, when I change a gameplay behaviour I want an explicit rule telling me to apply it consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, so I do not silently introduce drift.
  - *"As a developer, when I change a player/enemy/projectile/power-up behaviour I want to know the gyms are the parity reference, so I update both in the same change."*
- **As a producer/reviewer**, when I audit a gameplay change I want a documented rule to point to, so I can verify parity was considered.
  - *"As the producer, I want gym parity stated in AGENTS.md so it is enforceable in review, not just implicit in architecture notes."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `AGENTS.md` contains an explicit gym-parity rule stating that gyms are the canonical parity reference for the game and that any gameplay-behaviour change must be applied consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, unless a documented reason exists to diverge.
- **AC2** — The rule names the gym scenes/directories it applies to (at minimum `src/scenes/gym/`, including `src/scenes/gym/core/`, and the game-side scene/shared core such as `PlayScene` and `src/scenes/core/`), so a reader knows exactly which files are in scope.
- **AC3** — A docs review (grep/search across `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `docs/`) confirms there is no contradictory guidance that permits gyms to intentionally diverge without a documented reason; any near-conflicts are reconciled or explicitly noted.
- **AC4** — Validation: a reviewer can quote the AC1 rule from the rendered `AGENTS.md` and confirm it matches the producer directive; automated check is a grep asserting the rule text and the named directories are present.
- **AC5** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive only.** Do not weaken, reorder or remove any existing workflow/safety rule in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Consistent with existing architecture notes.** The rule must agree with the existing "Architecture Notes for Agents" shared-core description (no production scene keeps a divergent copy).
- **Docs-only change.** No application behaviour or source code behaviour changes.
- **UK English** spelling throughout.
- **Placement:** `AGENTS.md` currently has no "Game Architecture Conventions" or "Coding Disciplines" heading, so the rule is expected to be a new short section (e.g. `## Game Architecture Conventions`) placed near the existing `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section; final heading/placement is an implementation decision.

## Existing state

- `AGENTS.md` (repo-local) documents the agent workflow and Worklog usage, plus an `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section describing the shared two-tier combat core (`CombatCoreScene` → `CombatScene`) and the shared drop/bullet/enemy-fire layers. It states scenes must not keep divergent copies but has no explicit gym-parity rule.
- The gym scenes live in `src/scenes/gym/` (`GymBoss`, `GymCurveSequencer`, `GymEnemies`, `GymMinerals`, `GymPlayer`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeapons`) with the generic base `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`; the dev index is `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` and discovery is directory-dynamic via `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- `README.md` documents the gym index as a dev-mode playground; `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` is the authoritative gym/enemy guide and already treats the shared core as the mechanism for parity.
- The wider parity effort is tracked by the epic **Gym↔game behavioural parity (AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA)** and the in-progress **Extend parity regression guard and cross-scene equivalence tests (AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB)**.

## Desired change

Add a short, explicit rule to the repo-local `AGENTS.md` stating:

> Gyms are the canonical parity reference for the game. Any gameplay behaviour change must be applied consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, unless a documented reason exists to diverge.

The rule should name the gym scenes/directories it applies to (`src/scenes/gym/`) and the game-side scene/shared core (`PlayScene`, `src/scenes/core/`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS.md` — Add a new `## Game Architecture Conventions` section (or equivalent) containing the gym-parity rule; place near `## Architecture Notes for Agents`.
- `src/scenes/gym/` — The gym scene directory the rule names as in-scope (AC2); includes `core/GymFormationScene.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — The shared core the parity rule points to.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Generic gym base consuming the shared core.
- `README.md` — References the gym index; verify the new rule does not contradict it (AC3).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Authoritative gym guide; verify consistency (AC3).

## Related work

- **Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining core-code duplication so every object behaves identically (AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA)** — parent epic; this documentation rule supports its enforcement.
- **Extend parity regression guard and cross-scene equivalence tests (AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB)** — in-progress automated parity guard this rule complements.
- **Speed power up should increase all speeds (AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB)** — `discovered-from`; the parity-drift incident that motivated this item.
- **Document scheme-aware gym controls (AH-0MTFRQR42009TYE9)** — precedent docs-only gym change.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — authoritative guide for gym/enemy implementation.
- `AGENTS.md` § *Architecture Notes for Agents* — existing shared-core guidance to remain consistent with.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUAYB4EJ005CIYQ** – Power Ups scene title in index page (completed)
- **AH-0MUII3CXX0023H24** – Shared power-up drop layer (spawner, lifecycle, collection, magnet, P4 notice, cues) (completed)
- **AH-0MT94ULUU001NBW3** – Audit merge gate hard-codes npm run build; docs-only repos fail Phase 1 (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, acceptance, add, agents, always (+52 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, add, agents, always, anywhere (+46 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, add, always (+38 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The producer directive in the work item ("gyms are the canonical parity reference") is authoritative and should be quoted essentially verbatim.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Reconciling unrelated architecture-note content in `AGENTS.md` is out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items instead.
- **Risk (contradiction):** AC3 may surface pre-existing text that reads as permitting divergence; if found, note it on the work item rather than silently rewriting architecture notes.
- **Risk (enforcement gap):** A docs rule alone does not enforce parity — the automated guard (AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB) is the enforcement mechanism; this rule is the human/agent-facing complement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required. The seed context supplied the exact rule text, the acceptance criteria and the verification performed; all remaining facts (gym directory, game-side scene, related parity work) were obtained from repo/worklog search, per the interview contract's "do not ask questions answerable by repo search" rule.
- **OPEN QUESTION:** none.
- Research summary: `src/scenes/gym/` confirmed as the gym scene directory (`GymFormationScene.ts` under `core/`); `AGENTS.md` headings confirmed to contain no gym-parity rule and no "Coding Disciplines"/"Game Architecture Conventions" heading; the parity epic AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA (stage `plan_complete`) and guard AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB (in-progress) confirmed as related work.

---

## Plan review (@plan, auto-complete path)

Effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: skip` (effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low**), so this docs-only item is small enough to implement directly and no child decomposition was created. The six automated review stages were run against the existing content:

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — all six ACs trace to the Desired change and Constraints, and every requirement has a corresponding AC (rule text → AC1; in-scope directories → AC2; docs consistency → AC3; verification → AC4; related docs → AC5; suite → AC6). No missing, contradictory or invented ACs.
2. **Completeness** — description and `## Acceptance Criteria` present; the `**Key Files (predicted)**` section is syntactically valid (`validate_key_files_format` reports no issues / `validate_key_files_in_description` is empty) and every listed path exists (`AGENTS.md`, `src/scenes/gym/`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`, `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — no children and no dependency edges; this is a single docs work unit. The AC4 grep verification is to be added together with the `AGENTS.md` edit so it fails before and passes after.
4. **Scope sizing** — one deliverable increment (a short `AGENTS.md` section + the AC3 docs-consistency review + the AC4 grep assertion). No further breakdown needed.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — AC1/AC2 are pass/fail via the AC4 grep assertion; AC3/AC5 are documentation reviews; AC6 is the full suite. No criterion was so vague that it needed rewriting.
6. **Polish & handoff** — description is clear, well formatted and actionable; UK English throughout.

### Clarifications recorded during review (additive; no intent change)

- **Factual correction to Existing state / Constraints.** The intake brief states that the repo-local `AGENTS.md` `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section "describes the shared two-tier combat core" and "states scenes must not keep divergent copies". Verified this is **not** in `AGENTS.md` (`grep -c 'CombatCoreScene\|Gym' AGENTS.md` → 0). The shared-combat-core narrative lives in `README.md` (the "Shared combat core" / shared-layer notes around lines 361–397) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; the `AGENTS.md` `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section covers the Worklog data-storage architecture only.
  - *Impact:* none for the core deliverable — the rule is still added to `AGENTS.md`, and "place near `## Architecture Notes for Agents`" remains valid. The AC3 consistency check must therefore be run against `README.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, both of which already state that the game and gyms must not keep divergent copies (i.e. they are aligned, not contradictory).
- **AC5 scope.** There is no docs site or wiki in this repository (only `README.md` and `docs/*.md`), so AC5's "wiki or docs site entries" clause is a no-op; the in-scope related docs are `README.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

### AC coverage review

`run_coverage_review(AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1)` → `recommendation: proceed` (no children; all parent ACs are self-covered).

### Appendix — clarifying questions & answers (planning session)

- No new clarifying questions were required: the seed context and ACs are unambiguous, and the only findings were repo-search facts (recorded above). Existing Appendix entries are preserved unchanged; none needed re-asking.

# Create CombatCoreScene shared base class with stub-subclass tests

## Summary

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatCoreScene.ts` exists at `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` as a concrete class extending `Phaser.Scene` (or the existing scene base).
- [ ] **AC2** — `CombatCoreScene` owns: `_readPlayerInput` (input mapping + cursor/WASD/handler fields), `_autoFire` (auto-fire + `spawnPlayerBullet` + `onWeaponFired` hook), `_collectDrop` (drop collection + animation helpers + pickup cues via `_playPickupCue` hook), and the player-explosion/collect registries.
- [ ] **AC3** — `CombatCoreScene` declares the new hooks: `getInvulnerabilityDuration()` (default 1.5 s), `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (default no-op), `isPlayerPhased()` (default false), `onWeaponFired()` (default no-op), `_playPickupCue(type)` (default no-op), `onPowerUpCollected(powerUpType)` (default no-op).

- [ ] **AC5** — Existing tests still pass when `CombatScene` temporarily still extends `Phaser.Scene` (i.e. `CombatCoreScene` is added but `CombatScene` has not yet been refactored).
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — Implements parent AC1: [ ] **AC1 — Single shared definition of the eight methods.** Across all production scene files, each of `_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport` and `_readPlayerInput` is defined exactly once, in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` and/or `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`). ## Summary
Make `CombatScene` extend `CombatCoreScene` (instead of `Phaser.Scene` directly), moving the input, auto-fire, and drop-collection methods into the base class. `CombatScene` keeps the combat-specific template methods (`_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_handleTeleport`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`) and the enemy/bullet participant contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatScene` extends `CombatCoreScene` and no longer defines `_readPlayerInput`, `_autoFire`, or `_collectDrop`.
- [ ] **AC2** — `CombatScene` still defines the combat-only template methods: `_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_handleTeleport`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`.
- [ ] **AC3** — `CombatScene.test.ts` passes without modification (same behaviour, same test coverage).
- [ ] **AC4** — The `getInvulnerabilityDuration` hook is in `CombatCoreScene` with default 1.5 s; `CombatScene` uses it in the hit logic (no change from current default).
- [ ] **AC5** — `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` still work correctly (they extend `CombatScene`).
- [ ] **AC6** — `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass, preserving its cross-scene behavioural equivalence assertions for the shared paths.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — Implements parent AC1: [ ] **AC1 — Single shared definition of the eight methods.** Across all production scene files, each of `_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport` and `_readPlayerInput` is defined exactly once, in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` and/or `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`). Verified by extending the existing `definesMethod` guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` to scan every production scene file repo-wide.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — Implements parent AC6: [ ] **AC6 — Shared-core validation coverage.** The newly shared seams (auto-fire cue, drop collection/cue, input mapping, and the `getInvulnerabilityDuration` hook) are covered by base-class stub-subclass tests; cross-scene behavioural equivalence for the shared paths remains asserted by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
